chapters.title: Chapter 210: The Psycho Wife
paragraphs: Rather than answering, the system responded in its own way.
[Calculating previous day’s emotions...]
His eyes remained fixed on the floating dots, each passing second feeling like a countdown to his impending doom.
At the same time, he could clearly feel Aurielle’s arms tightening—slowly, almost imperceptibly—around his neck.
Just enough to remind him that his life currently depended on his next few words.
[Emotions Calculated: Angry / Jealous / Wants to strangle someone’s neck.]
Luke’s mouth twitched.
’System you added that last one yourself, didn’t you?’
Naturally, the system ignored his accusation.
Instead, another notification appeared.
[New Emotion Detected: *Natal Obsession.*]
[Please develop this emotion completely to unlock the next milestone.]
Luke’s expression immediately turned blank.
’You’ve got to be kidding me.’
He could already feel Aurielle’s fingers slowly tightening around his neck.
And the system wanted him to develop that emotion even further?
’System if you’re upset with me for something, just say it.’
’Don’t gamble with my life like this, buddy.’
Luke’s face immediately darkened.
"System who asked you to show me that?"
The System, however, acted as though it hadn’t heard a single word.
Instead, it silently enlarged the screen.
[Aurielle’s Thoughts:]
*So the womanizer title was actually accurate.*
*If he can’t give me one convincing reason for disappearing from our bed in the middle of the night.*
*And then returning with another woman.*
*I won’t let him off this time.*
’Ok, that’s some dangerous thought.’ Luke sighed slowly, because the system was even making him feel that he was having an affair behind his back.
Meanwhile, inside Lucy’s mind, another thought was going on.
’The psycho wife of Sir Luke.’ She thought about the rumors, how he had married five psycho wives who had never let any men touch them.
But now Sir Luke was handling all of them.
Aurora, who was hiding behind one of the bushes, saw all of this. That how her innocent master would be sacrificed by that crazy woman.
And if she knew Lucy’s thought, she would totally agree with her.
At this time, Luke’s gaze turned and met her for a moment. Hope was born in Luke’s heart.
That Aurora could save him, but Aurora turned her gaze away from him.
’Sorry, master. I don’t want to attend those bad Noble etiquette classes.’ So she sacrificed her master to the crazy woman.
Seeing this, Luke’s eyes filled with betrayal, but no one could come to help him.
As on one tall tree, Vaelira was calmly sitting and was adding another name to her list.
’Lucy Dawnwale, master’s another victim of the womanizer.’
"Master’s womanizer skills seem to have developed, even those outside people are talking about this title."
She muttered under her breath with a thoughtful expression.
But she didn’t know that there was Sophia as well, or another name would be added to that list.
Well, it would be in the future, even if it missed this time.
Luke realized there was no one else around. Letting out a small, helpless smile, he replied in the gentlest voice he could manage.
"Honey, I was just patrolling the territory."
"Ohh~ And why would the great lord personally patrol his territory, in the middle of the dead of night~?"
Her sweet, drawn-out tone sent a chill down Luke’s spine.
Danger.
His instincts screamed at him.
He didn’t hesitate. He chose the simplest. And most effective solution.
"Eek!"
Aurielle let out a startled yelp as Luke suddenly swept her off her feet into a princess carry.
"W-Wait—Luke!"
WHOOSH!
Before she could finish, his figure blurred, carrying her straight toward their house.
Aurora watched the direction they had disappeared for a few seconds before shaking her head.
"Master is going to do that thing again, the one that makes that crazy woman keep shouting in all kinds of voices."
She muttered under her breath.
Fortunately.
No one else heard her.
Finally, after several hours of coaxing, apologizing, and an exhausting amount of "hard work," in the bed. Which wet the whole bedsheet, Luke managed to calm Aurielle down.
She now lay quietly on the bed, sleeping peacefully, not a single complaint leaving her lips anymore.
"Huff..." Luke let out a long breath before getting out of bed.
"She lasted much longer this time." A surprised expression appeared on his face.
’Looks like after failing to find me, she spent quite a while training inside the Time Chamber.’ Luke thought to himself as he headed toward the bath.
"System, since Aurielle unlocked a new emotion, shouldn’t I receive a better reward this time?" he asked hopefully.
The system’s mocking voice immediately echoed in his mind.
[Oh?]
[Wasn’t someone saying earlier that he didn’t want her to become obsessive?]
[And now you’re asking for rewards?]
Luke’s footsteps paused. "That’s different."
[Different how?]
Luke coughed awkwardly. "I was speaking from a purely objective perspective."
[Sure you were.]
Luke silently decided that arguing with the system was a complete waste of time.
"Ahem." So he coughed lightly, trying to dispel the awkwardness.
The system ignored his reaction and calmly answered his question.
[That emotion has not fully matured yet.]
[Only after it completely develops will the corresponding rewards be granted.]
Hearing that, Luke’s eyelid twitched.
’So I got excited for nothing?’
He felt as though the system had deliberately tricked him.
Just as he was about to argue. Another notification suddenly appeared before his eyes.
[10x Return Activated]
Reward: Greatswordsman (E-Rank Human Warrior) ×10 (×100 Basic Multiplier)
[REWARD DESCRIPTION]
"A tall warrior clad in full plate armor, wielding a greatsword as tall as a grown man. Slow but unstoppable. Every swing cuts through enemies like wheat before a scythe."
"Hmm..." Luke rubbed his chin thoughtfully, his earlier dissatisfaction disappearing almost instantly.
"That actually looks pretty useful."
As it seemed the system was increasing the variety of its rewards.
Then his gaze shifted to the upgrade option as he weighed the two choices.
One thousand Bronze Knights? or ten Silver Knights?
He still had the option to upgrade the reward.

After thinking for a moment, Luke recalled the current state of his army. He already possessed a large number of Iron Knights, and after spending time training inside the Time Chamber, many of them were already on the verge of breaking through to the Bronze Knight realm.
On top of that, the Iron Knight Tempering Potions were accelerating their progress even further.
’Bronze Knights, I’ll have plenty of them soon.’
’Silver Knights, however, were a different story.’
He nodded to himself.

sentences.text: Rather than answering, the system responded in its own way.
[Calculating previous day’s emotions...]
His eyes remained fixed on the floating dots, each passing second feeling like a countdown to his impending doom.
At the same time, he could clearly feel Aurielle’s arms tightening—slowly, almost imperceptibly—around his neck.
Just enough to remind him that his life currently depended on his next few words.
[Emotions Calculated: Angry / Jealous / Wants to strangle someone’s neck.]
Luke’s mouth twitched.
’System you added that last one yourself, didn’t you?’
Naturally, the system ignored his accusation.
Instead, another notification appeared.
[New Emotion Detected: *Natal Obsession.*]
[Please develop this emotion completely to unlock the next milestone.]
Luke’s expression immediately turned blank.
’You’ve got to be kidding me.’
He could already feel Aurielle’s fingers slowly tightening around his neck.
And the system wanted him to develop that emotion even further?
’System if you’re upset with me for something, just say it.’
’Don’t gamble with my life like this, buddy.’
Luke’s face immediately darkened.
"System who asked you to show me that?"
The System, however, acted as though it hadn’t heard a single word.
Instead, it silently enlarged the screen.
[Aurielle’s Thoughts:]
*So the womanizer title was actually accurate.*
*If he can’t give me one convincing reason for disappearing from our bed in the middle of the night.*
*And then returning with another woman.*
*I won’t let him off this time.*
’Ok, that’s some dangerous thought.’ Luke sighed slowly, because the system was even making him feel that he was having an affair behind his back.
Meanwhile, inside Lucy’s mind, another thought was going on.
’The psycho wife of Sir Luke.’ She thought about the rumors, how he had married five psycho wives who had never let any men touch them.
But now Sir Luke was handling all of them.
Aurora, who was hiding behind one of the bushes, saw all of this.
That how her innocent master would be sacrificed by that crazy woman.
And if she knew Lucy’s thought, she would totally agree with her.
At this time, Luke’s gaze turned and met her for a moment.
Hope was born in Luke’s heart.
That Aurora could save him, but Aurora turned her gaze away from him.
’Sorry, master.
I don’t want to attend those bad Noble etiquette classes.’ So she sacrificed her master to the crazy woman.
Seeing this, Luke’s eyes filled with betrayal, but no one could come to help him.
As on one tall tree, Vaelira was calmly sitting and was adding another name to her list.
’Lucy Dawnwale, master’s another victim of the womanizer.’
"Master’s womanizer skills seem to have developed, even those outside people are talking about this title."
She muttered under her breath with a thoughtful expression.
But she didn’t know that there was Sophia as well, or another name would be added to that list.
Well, it would be in the future, even if it missed this time.
Luke realized there was no one else around.
Letting out a small, helpless smile, he replied in the gentlest voice he could manage.
"Honey, I was just patrolling the territory."
"Ohh~ And why would the great lord personally patrol his territory, in the middle of the dead of night~?"
Her sweet, drawn-out tone sent a chill down Luke’s spine.
Danger.
His instincts screamed at him.
He didn’t hesitate.
He chose the simplest.
And most effective solution.
"Eek!"
Aurielle let out a startled yelp as Luke suddenly swept her off her feet into a princess carry.
"W-Wait—Luke!"
WHOOSH!
Before she could finish, his figure blurred, carrying her straight toward their house.
Aurora watched the direction they had disappeared for a few seconds before shaking her head.
"Master is going to do that thing again, the one that makes that crazy woman keep shouting in all kinds of voices."
She muttered under her breath.
Fortunately.
No one else heard her.
Finally, after several hours of coaxing, apologizing, and an exhausting amount of "hard work," in the bed.
Which wet the whole bedsheet, Luke managed to calm Aurielle down.
She now lay quietly on the bed, sleeping peacefully, not a single complaint leaving her lips anymore.
"Huff..." Luke let out a long breath before getting out of bed.
"She lasted much longer this time." A surprised expression appeared on his face.
’Looks like after failing to find me, she spent quite a while training inside the Time Chamber.’ Luke thought to himself as he headed toward the bath.
"System, since Aurielle unlocked a new emotion, shouldn’t I receive a better reward this time?" he asked hopefully.
The system’s mocking voice immediately echoed in his mind.
[Oh?]
[Wasn’t someone saying earlier that he didn’t want her to become obsessive?]
[And now you’re asking for rewards?]
Luke’s footsteps paused.
"That’s different."
[Different how?]
Luke coughed awkwardly.
"I was speaking from a purely objective perspective."
[Sure you were.]
Luke silently decided that arguing with the system was a complete waste of time.

The system ignored his reaction and calmly answered his question.

chapters.title: Chapter 211: Seven Days Outside, 210 Inside
paragraphs: Although Silver Knights looked insignificant when compared to Golden Knights, they were the true backbone of any powerful force.

As Golden Knights rarely left their territories unless something major happened, whereas Silver Knights handled nearly everything—from leading armies and suppressing beast tides to escorting caravans and carrying out important missions.
"So it’s decided. Silver Knights."
Without any hesitation, Luke selected the Upgrade option.
Still there was one small regret.
These were ordinary soldiers, not elite units.
That meant they possessed no Origin Skills.
[SYSTEM NOTIFICATION]
*Reward Upgraded: Berserker Greatswordsman (D-Rank)*
*Bloodline Integration Applied*
*Unit Type: Bloodline Warrior*
[UNIT PROFILE]
Berserker Greatswordsman — D-Rank (Bloodline Warrior)
Rank: D-Rank (Silver Knight Equivalent)
Type: Bloodline Warrior
Role: Shock Troop / Frontline Breaker
Weapon: Massive Greatsword (Enchanted)
Armor: Heavy Plate Armor (Reduced for Mobility)
[BLOODLINE ABILITIES]
Passive: Frenzy Bloodline
- Damage increases the more HP they lose
- Cannot be stunned or knocked back
- Ignores pain
- Attack speed increases the longer they fight
Passive: Bloodrage
- Heals from kills
- Gains attack speed per kill
- Becomes more aggressive with each kill
[ACTIVE ABILITIES]
Frenzy Charge
- Charges forward with reckless speed
- Deals massive damage to enemies in the path
- Cannot be stopped or interrupted
Reckless Swing
- A wild, powerful swing that hits all enemies in a wide arc
- Deals bonus damage based on missing HP
- Breaks through shields
Berserker’s Roar
- Releases a terrifying roar
- Fears nearby enemies
- Buffs his own damage and speed
[ULTIMATE: DEATH RAGE]
Trigger: Drops below 20% HP
Effect:
- Damage tripled
- Speed doubled
- Heals from kills
- Every attack creates a shockwave
Aftermath: Collapses from exhaustion
[DEPLOYMENT CONFIRMATION]
You have 10 Berserker Greatswordsmen (D-Rank) — Bloodline Warriors.
Deploy them now?
- Yes → Added to your army.
- No → Remains in inventory.
"What the hell?" Luke raised his eyebrow, as he didn’t expect to get a lottery.
[o_O]
[You sure got lucky this time.]
Seeing the system’s reaction, a big grin appeared on Luke’s face.
As he was earlier reminiscing about not having elite units, but the upgrade made just now
though not fully elite, they were top-tier among normal units.
As they had bloodline abilities.
Other than Origin abilities and Ascension series, many beings are born with innate abilities.
And almost 99% of the time, it was related to their hidden bloodline or ancestral bloodline.
For Vampires and Royals, this was even more true.
Since their bloodline was linked with their Origin skill.
So the higher the bloodline awakening, the higher the chances of Origin skill rank.
But lower species who couldn’t awaken Origin skills because of insufficient bloodline
got some abilities of their ancestor’s origin, and this path was specially followed by beasts.
Whose bloodline purifies with each realm, and after 3-4 stages, they got the skill.
"Good." Luke nodded in satisfaction, as he read their description again, which clearly showed they were frontline warriors.
That could literally dominate the battlefield.
And regarding health issues, he had Elena for them, who could save them before they would die.
So he looked toward the options for deploy, but then he noticed he was inside the house. So he moved toward outside.
He successfully stepped outside since Aurielle was asleep and deployed them.
The next moment, ten silver magic circles bloomed before him, each radiating a brilliant metallic glow that illuminated the surroundings.
Whoom. Whoom. Whoom.
One after another, towering figures emerged from within the circles.
Each stood nearly eight feet tall, their massive, muscular frames wrapped in heavy enchanted armor that gleamed beneath the silver light. Resting in their hands were huge enchanted-grade greatswords.
Every one of them possessed the aura of an Early Silver Knight.
Thud! Thud! Thud!
Without the slightest hesitation, all ten warriors dropped to one knee in perfect unison.
Boom!
"MASTER!!!"
Their thunderous voices erupted together, echoing across the entire area like a battlefield war cry.
The powerful shout immediately drew attention.
Not far from the house, Aurora, Vaelira, Osric, and Margaret instinctively turned toward the source of the commotion.
Their eyes widened as they witnessed the newly summoned warriors.
’Master has summoned another group of powerful beings.’
The same thought surfaced in each of their minds.
However, before any of them could walk over and question him about the new units, Luke calmly gave his orders.
"Disperse. After some time, regroup and station yourselves at the safe house along the Ashveil Trade Route."
The Berserker Greatswordsmen bowed their heads.
"Yes, Master."
Although they spoke in a much more restrained tone this time, their naturally deep voices still carried an imposing force.
Without another word, the ten armored giants turned and departed in disciplined formation, their heavy footsteps gradually fading into the distance.
With that, Luke also departed for his training, leaving behind the wide-mouthed Osric and Edmund.
The two men remained rooted to the spot, staring at the retreating Berserker Greatswordsmen in utter disbelief.
Their towering eight-foot physiques were already intimidating enough, yet what truly left them speechless were the huge greatswords resting upon their shoulders.
Each blade measured nearly 2.3 meters in length.
Osric subconsciously compared the weapon to his own sword before swallowing hard.
’Can I even lift something like that without using Aether?’
The thought flashed through his mind as a stunned expression spread across his face.
After all, he himself had only recently stepped into the Early Silver Knight Realm.
7 days later, 10th of Flora Month, same year...
Luke lowered his gaze to the report resting on his desk as the faint chatter of people echoed throughout the office building.
Although only seven days had passed in the outside world, two hundred and ten days had already elapsed within the Time Chamber.
He pushed those thoughts aside and returned his attention to the report.
"The road to Windmarch Reach has been completed."
A satisfied smile appeared on his face.
After all, it would now allow his army to move swiftly between the two territories whenever needed, greatly improving logistics and military response.
Continuing down the report, his expression became thoughtful.
The reconstruction of the 1,000-kilometer Ashveil Trade Route had unfortunately fallen behind schedule.
So far, only the first 100 kilometers, stretching northward from his territory, had been completed.
Even that achievement had only been possible because tens of thousands of laborers had been deployed to the project simultaneously.
As during those seven days, Blackstone’s popularity had soared.
Part of the reason was Luke himself and his titles, coupled with his strength as a Mid-Golden Knight, had spread throughout the surrounding territories.
The other reason was the constant influx of merchant caravans and adventurer parties, both of which brought unprecedented activity to the once-quiet territory.

As a result, the four association branches also flourished, introducing goods, services, and resources that had never before been available in Blackstone. Their presence further boosted both investment and immigration.
The outcome was immediate.
Land prices throughout Blackstone skyrocketed.

chapters.title: Chapter 212: The Mysterious Powerhouse Of Blackstone
paragraphs: Even so, demand continued to exceed supply. More and more people chose to settle permanently, while merchants, adventurers, and travelers arrived every day, filling the streets with life.
Because of this explosive growth, Luke was forced to begin his expansion plan far earlier than expected.
Construction had already started toward the northern side of Blackstone, where the terrain rose into a higher slope than the current settlement.
Once completed, the expanded district would not only accommodate the rapidly growing population but also provide enough space for future markets, residences, and military facilities.
The defensive wall encircling Blackstone’s 1-kilometer territory had also been completed.
He also recall the commotion he had created on that time.
Originally, it stood only twenty feet high.
Luke, however, wasn’t satisfied.
A few days later, he quietly left the territory and transformed into his Cosmic Heart Titan. Using Elythos’ Cosmic Construct ability, he silently reshaped the entire defensive wall.

Without damaging a single section, the massive stone barrier rose from twenty feet to thirty feet in height. At the same time, using dense materials of his cosmic system, he condensed them within the structure, reinforcing every layer until the wall became far sturdier than before.
By the time Luke finished.
Even an Early Golden Knight would struggle to breach it.
The moment the transformation was complete—
RUMBLE!!!
The entire Blackstone Territory trembled violently.
The sudden earthquake terrified both the old residents and the countless newcomers.
"W-What’s happening?!"
"An earthquake?!"
"No it’s a landslide!"
Panic spread through the streets as people rushed outside, many believing the nearby Stormhowl Mountains had collapsed and were about to bury Blackstone.
Fortunately the shaking lasted only a short while.
As everyone cautiously looked toward the city walls.
Silence fell.
Their eyes slowly widened.
"T-The wall! It got taller?"
"And thicker?"
The defensive wall surrounding Blackstone had somehow risen by another ten feet. Not only that, but its surface had also become noticeably darker and denser, radiating a sense of unshakable solidity.
The sight left people dumbfounded.
Unable to comprehend what had happened, everyone eventually reached the same conclusion.
"It must’ve been Lady Tara!"
"She is the only Earth Mage in the territory!"
"It has to be her!"
Within a single day, Tara’s reputation exploded throughout Blackstone.
Rumors spread one after another, each more exaggerated than the last, until the entire territory acknowledged her with a brand-new title—
*The Mysterious Powerhouse of Blackstone Territory.*
Even the four Mid-Golden Knights representing the associations were startled by the sudden commotion.
After all, Blackstone already had Aurora Valcrest, an Early Golden Knight powerhouse, guarding the territory.
Now.
Another mysterious powerhouse had seemingly revealed themselves.
Naturally, all four associations immediately raised Blackstone’s danger assessment by another level.
Luke himself was equally speechless after hearing the rumors.
"Sure." He simply let everyone continue believing Tara was responsible.
It saved him the trouble of explaining anything.
Unfortunately, reshaping an entire city’s defensive wall wasn’t without a price.

Luke had pushed the Cosmic Heart Titan far beyond its current limits. The enormous Aether consumption had almost break his body completely, forcing him to spend the next few days recovering inside the Healing Spring.
During that time. He received a thorough scolding from Aurielle.
"You really don’t know how to take care of yourself."
"What if something had happened to you?"
"Did you even stop to think about me?"
"There are plenty of people in the territory who can handle these things."
"You don’t have to shoulder everything yourself."
She lectured him from morning until evening without giving him a chance to escape.
Luke could only smile wryly and apologize over and over again, offering thousands of kisses before she finally forgave him.
Only then did Aurielle’s expression soften.
As for the two of them.
They ended up spending the next few days, together in the Healing Spring, enjoying a rare period of peace before Blackstone’s next storm arrived.
That wasn’t the only astonishing event to shake Blackstone during those seven days.
Another incident drew even greater attention.
Beside the Ashveil Route, a colossal crater had been discovered.
It stretched nearly fifty kilometers across and plunged over ten kilometers into the earth.
It was the very place where the Ancient Temple had once stood. The place where Nyx had unleashed his power.
Naturally, no one knew that.
To the outside world, the gigantic crater had appeared overnight without any warning.
The discovery immediately ignited the curiosity of adventurers.
"An ancient ruin has appeared!"
"There has to be a hidden inheritance down there!"
"No natural landslide could create something like this."
Rumors spread like wildfire, and within days, adventurers, mercenary companies, tomb raiders, treasure hunters, and explorers from every direction began pouring into Blackstone.
Even the four Mid-Golden Knight managers representing the associations personally investigated the site.
For several consecutive days, they searched every corner of the enormous crater.
Yet...
They found absolutely nothing.
Only an impossibly vast crater that seemed as though a god had scooped away an entire section of the world.
Ironically, their failure only fueled even more speculation.
If four Mid-Golden Knights couldn’t uncover its secret. Then perhaps the real treasure was simply hidden deeper.
That single thought attracted even more people to Blackstone.

Even now, one could see adventurers, mercenaries, treasure hunters, tomb raiders, and explorers descending into the gigantic crater every single day, convinced that somewhere within its endless depths, an ancient secret was waiting to be discovered.
"They still haven’t come to meet me."
Luke lightly tapped his finger against the table, his brows furrowing as he thought about the four association managers.

Since Blackstone’s rapid expansion, the Alchemist Association, Blacksmith Association, and Merchant Guild had all begun transporting new resources and products into the territory, clearly intending to expand their businesses.
Only the Adventurer Guild remained largely unchanged, continuing its operations as though nothing unusual had happened.
There was, however, one piece of information that had caught Luke’s attention.
"The Tigris woman the Adventurer Guild’s branch master is a complete battle fanatic."
Luke let out a helpless sigh.
She had even come personally to challenge him to a duel.
Aurora had stepped forward before Luke could respond.
"I’ll handle her."
Those had been Aurora’s exact words.
Remembering that scene, Luke couldn’t help rubbing his forehead.
"I probably shouldn’t have let her go..."
But he allowed on that time, since he thought that maybe the guild master would be some early Golden Knight.
But at that time, Aurora said some chunibyo-like line in front of her.
"My master is high above the heavens and he doesn’t have time to deal with a pesky tiger woman."
"As my master has me."
This brought another rumor about him, that even the territory’s own powerhouse had fallen into the hands of the womanizer hero, Luke.
Some people even started calling him Womanizer Luke, rather than Hero Luke or Baron Luke, in silence.
For that, he had to hide from Aurielle for few days, as she was shouting while finding him. "You were the one who told her for sure."
"As she is innocent."
Yeah, Aurora was innocent, he knew, but her husband was even more innocent.
At that, he cursed the system, "System, because of all that obsessive things, this is happening."
Yeah, her behavior was changing much from that moment, as she was hardly able to tolerate any other women near him.
And the whole night, she also didn’t let him separate alone, which brought problems for his training.
So he had to send a clone for training and let Aurielle use his body as a teddy bear.
At that time, he even thought that bringing a teddy bear would work.
But the next moment he canceled that plan. As in yandere novels, the teddy bear suffers first, then comes the real husband’s turn.
"Haa..." He inhaled, before thinking about Aurora.
Aurora and Raya, the guild master of the Adventurer Guild, had become friends.
As after Aurora said those words, Raya was provoked, and they fought for days in the mountains.
Using only physical strength.
Which was also the perk of Golden Knights, who had huge stamina compared to Silver Knights.
That fight amazed many people, because they came to understand that Raya Tempest was a mid-golden knight level.
But Aurora was able to fight with little bit of losing.
Which brought another gossip to Blackstone, that the four association masters were all mid-golden knights.
"Mid-Golden knight." Luke muttered thoughtfully.
If it was before his Nexus Titan, then he would definitely be worried.
But now he didn’t fear them much. Of course, their danger to the territory still held.
After all, if a fight occurred here, then the territory would not survive.
As he was thinking this, he heard a voice from outside. "Master, I am going to play with Raya."
With that, Aurora left the Time Chamber.
"Sigh." Luke sighed, because he could guess how she almost fought with the mid-golden knight Raya.
"Because of her defense." He leaned back on the chair, as those words escaped his mouth.

Because of this explosive growth, Luke was forced to begin his expansion plan far earlier than expected.

Once completed, the expanded district would not only accommodate the rapidly growing population but also provide enough space for future markets, residences, and military facilities.
The defensive wall encircling Blackstone’s 1-kilometer territory had also been completed.
He also recall the commotion he had created on that time.
Originally, it stood only twenty feet high.
Luke, however, wasn’t satisfied.
A few days later, he quietly left the territory and transformed into his Cosmic Heart Titan.
Using Elythos’ Cosmic Construct ability, he silently reshaped the entire defensive wall.
Without damaging a single section, the massive stone barrier rose from twenty feet to thirty feet in height.
At the same time, using dense materials of his cosmic system, he condensed them within the structure, reinforcing every layer until the wall became far sturdier than before.
By the time Luke finished.
Even an Early Golden Knight would struggle to breach it.
The moment the transformation was complete—
RUMBLE!!!
The entire Blackstone Territory trembled violently.
The sudden earthquake terrified both the old residents and the countless newcomers.
"W-What’s happening?!"
"An earthquake?!"
"No it’s a landslide!"
Panic spread through the streets as people rushed outside, many believing the nearby Stormhowl Mountains had collapsed and were about to bury Blackstone.
Fortunately the shaking lasted only a short while.
As everyone cautiously looked toward the city walls.
Silence fell.
Their eyes slowly widened.
"T-The wall!
It got taller?"
"And thicker?"
The defensive wall surrounding Blackstone had somehow risen by another ten feet.
Not only that, but its surface had also become noticeably darker and denser, radiating a sense of unshakable solidity.
The sight left people dumbfounded.
Unable to comprehend what had happened, everyone eventually reached the same conclusion.
"It must’ve been Lady Tara!"
"She is the only Earth Mage in the territory!"
"It has to be her!"
Within a single day, Tara’s reputation exploded throughout Blackstone.
Rumors spread one after another, each more exaggerated than the last, until the entire territory acknowledged her with a brand-new title—
*The Mysterious Powerhouse of Blackstone Territory.*
Even the four Mid-Golden Knights representing the associations were startled by the sudden commotion.
After all, Blackstone already had Aurora Valcrest, an Early Golden Knight powerhouse, guarding the territory.
Now.
Another mysterious powerhouse had seemingly revealed themselves.
Naturally, all four associations immediately raised Blackstone’s danger assessment by another level.
Luke himself was equally speechless after hearing the rumors.
"Sure." He simply let everyone continue believing Tara was responsible.
It saved him the trouble of explaining anything.
Unfortunately, reshaping an entire city’s defensive wall wasn’t without a price.
Luke had pushed the Cosmic Heart Titan far beyond its current limits.
The enormous Aether consumption had almost break his body completely, forcing him to spend the next few days recovering inside the Healing Spring.
During that time.
He received a thorough scolding from Aurielle.
"You really don’t know how to take care of yourself."
"What if something had happened to you?"
"Did you even stop to think about me?"
"There are plenty of people in the territory who can handle these things."
"You don’t have to shoulder everything yourself."
She lectured him from morning until evening without giving him a chance to escape.
Luke could only smile wryly and apologize over and over again, offering thousands of kisses before she finally forgave him.
Only then did Aurielle’s expression soften.
As for the two of them.
They ended up spending the next few days, together in the Healing Spring, enjoying a rare period of peace before Blackstone’s next storm arrived.
That wasn’t the only astonishing event to shake Blackstone during those seven days.
Another incident drew even greater attention.
Beside the Ashveil Route, a colossal crater had been discovered.
It stretched nearly fifty kilometers across and plunged over ten kilometers into the earth.
It was the very place where the Ancient Temple had once stood.
The place where Nyx had unleashed his power.
Naturally, no one knew that.
To the outside world, the gigantic crater had appeared overnight without any warning.
The discovery immediately ignited the curiosity of adventurers.
"An ancient ruin has appeared!"
"There has to be a hidden inheritance down there!"
"No natural landslide could create something like this."
Rumors spread like wildfire, and within days, adventurers, mercenary companies, tomb raiders, treasure hunters, and explorers from every direction began pouring into Blackstone.
Even the four Mid-Golden Knight managers representing the associations personally investigated the site.
For several consecutive days, they searched every corner of the enormous crater.
Yet...
They found absolutely nothing.
Only an impossibly vast crater that seemed as though a god had scooped away an entire section of the world.
Ironically, their failure only fueled even more speculation.
If four Mid-Golden Knights couldn’t uncover its secret.
Then perhaps the real treasure was simply hidden deeper.
That single thought attracted even more people to Blackstone.

Even now, one could see adventurers, mercenaries, treasure hunters, tomb raiders, and explorers descending into the gigantic crater every single day, convinced that somewhere within its endless depths, an ancient secret was waiting to be discovered.
"They still haven’t come to meet me."
Luke lightly tapped his finger against the table, his brows furrowing as he thought about the four association managers.

Since Blackstone’s rapid expansion, the Alchemist Association, Blacksmith Association, and Merchant Guild had all begun transporting new resources and products into the territory, clearly intending to expand their businesses.
Only the Adventurer Guild remained largely unchanged, continuing its operations as though nothing unusual had happened.
There was, however, one piece of information that had caught Luke’s attention.
"The Tigris woman the Adventurer Guild’s branch master is a complete battle fanatic."
Luke let out a helpless sigh.
She had even come personally to challenge him to a duel.
Aurora had stepped forward before Luke could respond.
"I’ll handle her."
Those had been Aurora’s exact words.
Remembering that scene, Luke couldn’t help rubbing his forehead.
"I probably shouldn’t have let her go..."
But he allowed on that time, since he thought that maybe the guild master would be some early Golden Knight.
But at that time, Aurora said some chunibyo-like line in front of her.
"My master is high above the heavens and he doesn’t have time to deal with a pesky tiger woman."
"As my master has me."
This brought another rumor about him, that even the territory’s own powerhouse had fallen into the hands of the womanizer hero, Luke.
Some people even started calling him Womanizer Luke, rather than Hero Luke or Baron Luke, in silence.
For that, he had to hide from Aurielle for few days, as she was shouting while finding him.
"You were the one who told her for sure."
"As she is innocent."
Yeah, Aurora was innocent, he knew, but her husband was even more innocent.
At that, he cursed the system, "System, because of all that obsessive things, this is happening."
Yeah, her behavior was changing much from that moment, as she was hardly able to tolerate any other women near him.
And the whole night, she also didn’t let him separate alone, which brought problems for his training.
So he had to send a clone for training and let Aurielle use his body as a teddy bear.
At that time, he even thought that bringing a teddy bear would work.
But the next moment he canceled that plan.
As in yandere novels, the teddy bear suffers first, then comes the real husband’s turn.
"Haa..." He inhaled, before thinking about Aurora.
Aurora and Raya, the guild master of the Adventurer Guild, had become friends.
As after Aurora said those words, Raya was provoked, and they fought for days in the mountains.
Using only physical strength.
Which was also the perk of Golden Knights, who had huge stamina compared to Silver Knights.
That fight amazed many people, because they came to understand that Raya Tempest was a mid-golden knight level.
But Aurora was able to fight with little bit of losing.
Which brought another gossip to Blackstone, that the four association masters were all mid-golden knights.
"Mid-Golden knight." Luke muttered thoughtfully.
If it was before his Nexus Titan, then he would definitely be worried.
But now he didn’t fear them much.
Of course, their danger to the territory still held.
After all, if a fight occurred here, then the territory would not survive.
As he was thinking this, he heard a voice from outside.
"Master, I am going to play with Raya."
With that, Aurora left the Time Chamber.
"Sigh." Luke sighed, because he could guess how she almost fought with the mid-golden knight Raya.
"Because of her defense." He leaned back on the chair, as those words escaped his mouth.

chapters.title: Chapter 213: The Knights Waited For The Legendary Maid Skirt Flip Incident
paragraphs: With that, Luke rose from his chair and walked outside.
The moment he stepped out of the mansion, his eyes fell upon the two Berserk Greatswordsmen standing guard at the entrance to the Lord’s Estate.

Each stood nearly eight feet tall, their heavily muscled bodies encased in full plate armor. huge greatswords rested in their hands, while the faint pressure of an Early Silver Knight aura radiated from both of them, silently warning everyone to keep their distance.
Just their presence alone was enough to deter troublemakers.
When these warriors had first appeared, the entire territory had been thrown into confusion.
"Where did Baron Luke recruit another Silver Knight squad?"
"Ten Silver Knights just like that?"
The rumors spread for several days, but no one managed to uncover their origins.
Eventually, the residents accepted the simplest explanation.
With Blackstone attracting thousands of newcomers every day, everyone assumed they were merely another group of powerful recruits who had chosen to pledge their loyalty to Luke.
No one questioned it further.
Then...
Blackstone’s northern expansion reached the foothills of the Stormhowl Mountains.
And the beast tide arrived.
It was the very same beast tide that had originally been stirred up because of Luke’s earlier actions. Delayed by distance, it finally reached the outskirts of Blackstone.
The moment roars echoed from the mountains. Panic spread throughout the newly settled districts.
Among the surging horde were not only ordinary beasts but also Blood Awakening beasts—the equivalent of Silver Knights.
At that realm, beasts awakened fragments of their ancestral bloodlines.
Some gained overwhelming physical strength. Others wielded elemental abilities.
Some possessed poisonous blood, terrifying regeneration, or bizarre innate talents that made them far deadlier than ordinary magical beasts.

Just sensing the auras of those creatures was enough to make many civilians turn pale. Even experienced adventurers wore solemn expressions, knowing that a single Blood Awakening beast could easily slaughter an ordinary squad if left unchecked.
However, before the beast tide could even reach Blackstone’s newly expanded one-kilometer perimeter...
The ten Berserk Greatswordsmen moved.
Without waiting for orders. Without a hint of hesitation.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
The ground trembled as the towering warriors charged straight toward the oncoming horde, their huge greatswords dragging across the earth before being lifted onto their shoulders.
"W-What are they doing?!"
"They’re charging toward the beast tide?!"
"Are they insane?!"
The onlookers were left dumbfounded.
There were only ten of them.
Against a tide containing thousands of beasts, including several Blood Awakening monsters.
Even if every one of them was an Early Silver Knight, the numbers alone should have overwhelmed them.
And at first...
That was exactly what happened.
The beasts surged forward like a flood, surrounding the warriors from every direction.
Claws tore through armor. Fangs ripped into flesh.
Fresh wounds appeared across their bodies one after another.
Yet-
Not a single Greatswordsman retreated.
Not one of them cried out in pain.
They swung their huge blades again and again...
Like fearless berserkers who knew nothing but battle.
"They’re..."
"...completely reckless."
An adventurer muttered in disbelief.
But then something unbelievable happened.
Instead of growing weaker as blood flowed from their wounds.
The ten warriors began growing stronger.
A crimson glow gradually spread across their bodies.
FWOOM!
Their muscles swelled. Their auras surged.
Even the horrific wounds covering their bodies began healing at a speed visible to the naked eye.
"What?!"
"They’re getting stronger?!"
"How is that even possible?!"
Shock rippled through the crowd.
The more injuries the Berserk Greatswordsmen suffered. The fiercer they became.
It was as though pain itself had become their source of strength.
By the time the Blood Awakening beasts finally forced their way through the pile of corpses.
Every ordinary beast had already been slaughtered.
The battlefield had covered fully in blood.
The three Blood Awakening beasts let out furious roars and charged together.
ROARRR!!
The collision lasted only a few minutes.
Then silence returned.
The last Blood Awakening beast collapsed with a thunderous crash, its enormous body crashing into the blood-soaked earth.
The ten Berserk Greatswordsmen remained standing.
That battle became the talk of the entire territory.
Whether inside taverns. The Adventurer Guild. Merchant buildings.
Or the bustling marketplace. People spoke of only one thing.
"Never provoke Baron Luke’s Berserk Knights."
The warning spread from mouth to mouth until it became common knowledge throughout Blackstone.
Naturally, news of the battle also reached the ears of the four association branch masters.
They acknowledged it. But none of them showed much reaction.
After all...
In their eyes, they were still merely Early Silver Knights.
Impressive, certainly.
But not enough to make four Mid-Golden Knights truly take them seriously.
"Master!"
The moment Luke reached the gate, two Berserk Greatswordsmen saluted in unison.
Luke returned the greeting with a nod and a smile before walking out from the Lord’s Estate.
However, after only a few steps, he suddenly stopped.
Under his gaze, the maids looked unusually panicked, while the younger knights wore expressions full of anticipation.
’Wait? why are the maids panicking?’
’And why do those idiots look so excited?’
Frowning, Luke turned back to look at them.
The instant he did, several young knights’ eyes lit up.
Their gazes repeatedly shifted between Luke... and the frightened maids.
Luke’s mouth twitched.
’These bastards...’
He immediately understood what they were waiting for.
The legendary *Maid Skirt Flip Incident.*
’Not happening.’
Without giving them the show they were hoping for, Luke walked away.
Behind him, the young knights collectively lowered their heads in disappointment.
Meanwhile, the maids let out relieved sighs before shooting the dejected knights icy, murderous stares.
’The border issue has already been taken care of,’ Luke thought as he walked through the estate.
He had already dispatched two Silver Knights along with one hundred newly promoted Bronze Archer Knights to the western border, nearly 1,000 kilometers away.
Those archers were the same elite Peak Iron Knight soldiers as before. They had only advanced to Bronze because there weren’t enough Iron Breakthrough Potions for everyone earlier.
Their mission was straightforward—eliminate the roaming beasts and hostile tribes threatening the border, then return together with Taron, the Silver Knight who had been stationed there.
Thinking of Taron reminded Luke of his territory’s military progress.
The 5,000 Body Temper soldiers who had remained in Blackstone during the previous campaign had all successfully broken through to the Iron Knight realm.
Most of them were still in the Early Iron Knight stage, but that was already an huge improvement compared to before.
Their rapid growth was largely thanks to the immense concentration of Aether within the Time Chamber.
Months of uninterrupted training there had produced results that would have taken years under normal circumstances.

Even the ten Early Silver Knights of the Blackstone Legion had advanced significantly. As for Osric, he had already reached the Third Stage of the Silver Knight realm during this extended training period, the same as ten early silver knight.
Seeing such progress also made Luke realize just how much, Origin skill was helpful for cultivation.
It accelerated cultivation at an unbelievable rate.
Unfortunately, Osric and the previous silver knight didn’t posses this, or there realm would even higher.
The mages had also made remarkable progress.
Since Elena had already become a Circled Mage, equivalent to a Bronze Knight, the other talented mages under her guidance had likewise reached that realm.
As for Vaelira...
She had already stepped into the Half-Golden Knight stage.

chapters.title: Chapter 214: They Knew Him... for the Wrong Reason
paragraphs: According to Luke’s estimate, she needed roughly one more year of cultivation before she could officially break through into the Golden Knight realm.
"Even Aurielle has reached the Peak Bronze Knight realm and can already begin preparing for her breakthrough to Silver Knight," Luke muttered with a helpless sigh.
Thinking about everyone’s progress left him feeling slightly depressed.
Almost every one in Blackstone had advanced.
Yet when it came to cultivation. He was still an Early Bronze Knight.
His combat strength had increased by leaps and bounds thanks to his Titans, but his actual cultivation realm hadn’t moved an inch.
"F*ck that curse... or whatever the hell it is."
He couldn’t help but curse whoever had placed such a restriction on him.
"Haa..." After taking a deep breath to calm himself, Luke continued walking.
Before long, his eyes landed on a familiar figure wandering through the territory.
Peter Bassus.
Since it was his day off, Peter was leisurely strolling through Blackstone instead of training.
"Hmm..." Seeing him reminded Luke of Windmarch Reach.
Originally, he had planned to send Aurora there.
However, after Aurora became close friends with Raya, Luke had begun reconsidering that decision.
The two spent most of their time together, and separating them now didn’t seem necessary.
So, instead of sending Aurora, he dispatched Patrick, the newly joined Early Golden Knight, to Windmarch Reach.
After all, that territory currently didn’t have a single Golden Knight overseeing its defenses.
Even though Luke didn’t believe Patrick would betray him, he still had Patrick’s mother and younger brother remain in Blackstone.
It wasn’t meant as punishment.
It was simply a precaution.
Patrick himself didn’t find the arrangement strange.
Only Peter immediately understood the true reason behind it.
Even so, he never raised the issue.
Perhaps he understood that trust wasn’t something earned overnight.
Interestingly, throughout the past several days, Windmarch Reach hadn’t faced a single attack.
"Are they wary of the Holy Church or that hidden powerhouse?" Luke muttered thoughtfully.
As Luke walked past, Peter gave him a respectfull nod, which Luke returned with node before continuing on his way.
Although the reconstruction of the Ashveil Trade Route had yet to be fully completed, the essential infrastructure was already in place.
Safe stations had been established at regular intervals, patrol squads constantly guarded the road, and the territory’s escort service had officially begun operating.
As a result, soldiers assigned to escort missions were now granted a full day of rest after returning to Blackstone before receiving another assignment.
Thinking about the territory’s steady development, Luke continued toward his destination.
*The Silver Exchange — Merchant Guild Branch.*
The shipment he had purchased from Stormveil County had finally arrived shortly after his knights returned to Blackstone.
Even so, Blackstone’s demand for resources was growing faster than ever.
Weapons, armor, medicine, construction materials.
Every passing day, the territory consumed more than the last.
The army alone had recently expanded by another 10,000 Body Temper soldiers, 5,000 Iron Knights, and 500 Bronze Knights.
Most of those recruits were former mercenaries and adventurers, especially the Bronze Knights, who had been attracted by Blackstone’s rapid rise.
Even so, not a single Silver Knight had volunteered to join the territory.
The only exceptions remained the Bassus brothers.
Luke wasn’t particularly surprised.
After all, a Silver Knight could also commanded respect even within a Count’s territory.
Blackstone was still far from reaching that level.
Whether it was military strength, infrastructure, or overall influence, his territory still couldn’t compare to even an ordinary Viscount domain.
Many districts remained undeveloped, while facilities still existed only on paper.
Even so...
There was one piece of good news.
"At least Windmarch Reach is now completely under Blackstone’s control."
A satisfied smile appeared on Luke’s face.
After he had left the main army behind, his soldiers divided their forces and systematically secured every settlement across the territory.
Towns and Villages.
Even the remaining cities had all accepted Blackstone’s banner without further resistance.
During that time, Luke had also submitted an official request to Count Magnus for recognition of the newly acquired territory.
To his surprise...
The Count approved it without objection.
The official confirmation letter had arrived only yesterday.
"Greetings, Baron Luke."
The voices of two guards pulled him out of his thoughts.
Clad in polished silver armor, they saluted respectfully as they opened the entrance doors for him of the merchant building.
Luke gave them a calm nod before stepping inside.
The interior of the Silver Exchange was spacious and elegantly decorated.
Crystal chandeliers hung from the ceiling, illuminating the grand hall, while neatly arranged service counters were staffed by five or six female receptionists busily assisting customers.
The waiting area was equally crowded.
Merchants and adventurers occupied nearly every seat and sofa, discussing business among themselves.
However, the moment Luke stepped inside...
The entire hall gradually fell silent. Curious gazes immediately converged on him.
Some merchants subtly exchanged looks, their expressions saying exactly what was on their minds.
’That’s Baron Luke.’
’The infamous womanizer.’
Even the receptionists paused their work for a brief moment before turning toward the entrance.
Luke paid little attention to the sudden silence.
His identity alone was enough to draw attention wherever he went now.
As the lord of Blackstone, his name—and his presence—already carried considerable weight.
However.
If he ever found out that they were secretly calling him "the Womanizer of Blackstone,"
He was fairly certain he’d drag every single one of them outside for a "friendly" spar.
Fortunately for everyone present.
No one was foolish enough to say those words out loud.
"Where’s your manager?" Luke asked after stopping in front of one of the reception counters.
The young receptionist froze for a moment, clearly caught off guard that the Baron himself was speaking to her.
"U-Upstairs." she answered after quickly regaining her composure.
Before Luke could respond, a calm voice echoed from above.
"Baron Luke, my apologies for keeping you waiting."
A middle-aged man descended the staircase with steady steps.
He stood around six feet tall, with neatly combed black hair, a trimmed beard, and a well-maintained physique. His luxurious attire immediately revealed his high position within the Silver Exchange.
Reaching the bottom of the stairs, he offered a respectful bow.
"Sir, I am Jasper Merrick, manager of the Silver Exchange."
Luke acknowledged the greeting with a nod.
"Please, this way." Jasper personally led him upstairs.
They passed the second, third, fourth, and fifth floors before finally arriving at the sixth.
Unlike the bustling levels below, the entire top floor had been converted into an expansive VIP suite reserved for distinguished guests.
The VIP suite was lavishly decorated.
Gold-lined pillars, polished marble, and finely cut rubies adorned the room, giving it an air of understated luxury rather than excessive extravagance.
After both of them took their seats on opposite sofas, Jasper smiled warmly.
"Baron Luke, I’ve been looking forward to meeting you for quite some time."
Luke returned a polite nod.
"Likewise, Manager Jasper."
Sensing that Luke preferred to get straight to business, Jasper didn’t waste any more time on pleasantries.
"How may the Silver Exchange assist you today?"
Luke nodded.
"Manager Jasper, I’d like to place a bulk order."
Jasper’s smile widened slightly as he listened attentively.
"First, I need G-rank and F-rank spears, along with full-body armor of the same grades."
Those would be issued to the newly recruited soldiers.
Jasper silently noted everything down.
Luke continued.
"In addition, I need a large quantity of construction materials."
Until now, most of Blackstone’s construction materials had been supplied by small and medium-sized merchants.
However, with the territory expanding at an unprecedented pace, Luke knew that relying on them alone would no longer be enough.
The Silver Exchange was far better suited for large-scale procurement.

He couldn’t help but curse whoever had placed such a restriction on him.
"Haa..." After taking a deep breath to calm himself, Luke continued walking.
Before long, his eyes landed on a familiar figure wandering through the territory.
Peter Bassus.
Since it was his day off, Peter was leisurely strolling through Blackstone instead of training.
"Hmm..." Seeing him reminded Luke of Windmarch Reach.
Originally, he had planned to send Aurora there.
However, after Aurora became close friends with Raya, Luke had begun reconsidering that decision.
The two spent most of their time together, and separating them now didn’t seem necessary.
So, instead of sending Aurora, he dispatched Patrick, the newly joined Early Golden Knight, to Windmarch Reach.
After all, that territory currently didn’t have a single Golden Knight overseeing its defenses.
Even though Luke didn’t believe Patrick would betray him, he still had Patrick’s mother and younger brother remain in Blackstone.
It wasn’t meant as punishment.
It was simply a precaution.
Patrick himself didn’t find the arrangement strange.
Only Peter immediately understood the true reason behind it.
Even so, he never raised the issue.
Perhaps he understood that trust wasn’t something earned overnight.
Interestingly, throughout the past several days, Windmarch Reach hadn’t faced a single attack.
"Are they wary of the Holy Church or that hidden powerhouse?" Luke muttered thoughtfully.
As Luke walked past, Peter gave him a respectfull nod, which Luke returned with node before continuing on his way.
Although the reconstruction of the Ashveil Trade Route had yet to be fully completed, the essential infrastructure was already in place.
Safe stations had been established at regular intervals, patrol squads constantly guarded the road, and the territory’s escort service had officially begun operating.
As a result, soldiers assigned to escort missions were now granted a full day of rest after returning to Blackstone before receiving another assignment.
Thinking about the territory’s steady development, Luke continued toward his destination.
*The Silver Exchange — Merchant Guild Branch.*
The shipment he had purchased from Stormveil County had finally arrived shortly after his knights returned to Blackstone.
Even so, Blackstone’s demand for resources was growing faster than ever.
Weapons, armor, medicine, construction materials.
Every passing day, the territory consumed more than the last.
The army alone had recently expanded by another 10,000 Body Temper soldiers, 5,000 Iron Knights, and 500 Bronze Knights.
Most of those recruits were former mercenaries and adventurers, especially the Bronze Knights, who had been attracted by Blackstone’s rapid rise.
Even so, not a single Silver Knight had volunteered to join the territory.
The only exceptions remained the Bassus brothers.
Luke wasn’t particularly surprised.
After all, a Silver Knight could also commanded respect even within a Count’s territory.
Blackstone was still far from reaching that level.
Whether it was military strength, infrastructure, or overall influence, his territory still couldn’t compare to even an ordinary Viscount domain.
Many districts remained undeveloped, while facilities still existed only on paper.
Even so...
There was one piece of good news.
"At least Windmarch Reach is now completely under Blackstone’s control."
A satisfied smile appeared on Luke’s face.
After he had left the main army behind, his soldiers divided their forces and systematically secured every settlement across the territory.
Towns and Villages.
Even the remaining cities had all accepted Blackstone’s banner without further resistance.
During that time, Luke had also submitted an official request to Count Magnus for recognition of the newly acquired territory.
To his surprise...
The Count approved it without objection.
The official confirmation letter had arrived only yesterday.
"Greetings, Baron Luke."
The voices of two guards pulled him out of his thoughts.
Clad in polished silver armor, they saluted respectfully as they opened the entrance doors for him of the merchant building.
Luke gave them a calm nod before stepping inside.
The interior of the Silver Exchange was spacious and elegantly decorated.
Crystal chandeliers hung from the ceiling, illuminating the grand hall, while neatly arranged service counters were staffed by five or six female receptionists busily assisting customers.
The waiting area was equally crowded.
Merchants and adventurers occupied nearly every seat and sofa, discussing business among themselves.
However, the moment Luke stepped inside...
The entire hall gradually fell silent.
Curious gazes immediately converged on him.
Some merchants subtly exchanged looks, their expressions saying exactly what was on their minds.
’That’s Baron Luke.’
’The infamous womanizer.’
Even the receptionists paused their work for a brief moment before turning toward the entrance.
Luke paid little attention to the sudden silence.
His identity alone was enough to draw attention wherever he went now.
As the lord of Blackstone, his name—and his presence—already carried considerable weight.
However.
If he ever found out that they were secretly calling him "the Womanizer of Blackstone,"
He was fairly certain he’d drag every single one of them outside for a "friendly" spar.
Fortunately for everyone present.
No one was foolish enough to say those words out loud.
"Where’s your manager?" Luke asked after stopping in front of one of the reception counters.
The young receptionist froze for a moment, clearly caught off guard that the Baron himself was speaking to her.
"U-Upstairs." she answered after quickly regaining her composure.
Before Luke could respond, a calm voice echoed from above.
"Baron Luke, my apologies for keeping you waiting."
A middle-aged man descended the staircase with steady steps.
He stood around six feet tall, with neatly combed black hair, a trimmed beard, and a well-maintained physique.
His luxurious attire immediately revealed his high position within the Silver Exchange.
Reaching the bottom of the stairs, he offered a respectful bow.
"Sir, I am Jasper Merrick, manager of the Silver Exchange."
Luke acknowledged the greeting with a nod.
"Please, this way." Jasper personally led him upstairs.
They passed the second, third, fourth, and fifth floors before finally arriving at the sixth.
Unlike the bustling levels below, the entire top floor had been converted into an expansive VIP suite reserved for distinguished guests.
The VIP suite was lavishly decorated.
Gold-lined pillars, polished marble, and finely cut rubies adorned the room, giving it an air of understated luxury rather than excessive extravagance.
After both of them took their seats on opposite sofas, Jasper smiled warmly.
"Baron Luke, I’ve been looking forward to meeting you for quite some time."
Luke returned a polite nod.
"Likewise, Manager Jasper."
Sensing that Luke preferred to get straight to business, Jasper didn’t waste any more time on pleasantries.
"How may the Silver Exchange assist you today?"
Luke nodded.
"Manager Jasper, I’d like to place a bulk order."
Jasper’s smile widened slightly as he listened attentively.
"First, I need G-rank and F-rank spears, along with full-body armor of the same grades."
Those would be issued to the newly recruited soldiers.
Jasper silently noted everything down.
Luke continued.
"In addition, I need a large quantity of construction materials."
Until now, most of Blackstone’s construction materials had been supplied by small and medium-sized merchants.
However, with the territory expanding at an unprecedented pace, Luke knew that relying on them alone would no longer be enough.
The Silver Exchange was far better suited for large-scale procurement.

chapters.title: Chapter 215: Preparing for the Worst
paragraphs: After listening carefully, Jasper nodded.
"Is there anything else you require, Baron Luke?"
Luke shook his head.
The remaining supplies weren’t needed in such massive quantities, and the smaller merchants were more than capable of meeting that demand.
"Very well."
Jasper smiled confidently.
"I’ll make the necessary arrangements. Everything you’ve requested will be delivered as quickly as possible."
Luke nodded in satisfaction.
Just as he was about to stand and take his leave-
"Baron Luke."
Jasper called out with a meaningful smile.
Luke paused for a moment before calmly sitting back down on the sofa.
Then he gestured for him to continue.
Jasper inclined his head before speaking calmly.
"Baron Luke, our families who own the Silver Exchange have conducted business across Regnum for more than five hundred years."
*Regnum—the Human Continent of Valtharion.*
Luke gave a slight nod, silently listening.
Jasper folded his hands together and finally reached the true reason for stopping him.
"Because of that..."
"The Silver Exchange wishes to invest in you, Baron Luke."
Luke’s eyebrows rose slightly.
He understood exactly what Jasper meant by investment.
Rare elixirs. High-grade potions. Secret techniques. Powerful equipment.
Connections that stretched across the entire continent.
In short...
The Silver Exchange was offering to back Hero Luke’s rise.
Luke was already familiar with arrangements like this.
Merchant families rarely invested without expecting something in return.
If the Silver Exchange backed his rise, then as Luke’s become famous, so would the prestige and influence of the Silver Exchange.
It was a mutually beneficial partnership.
He also understood why they had approached him now.
His reputation had skyrocketed over the past few days, and the infamous "talentless" label had quietly disappeared from public opinion.
At least...
That was what the world believed.
To everyone else, he was a rising Hero with extraordinary potential but no major faction supporting him.
Naturally, they wanted to establish ties before someone else did.
Luke fell silent, carefully weighing the proposal while Jasper patiently waited for his answer.
’Resources won’t help my cultivation.’
’My Titan transformations already provide me with armor and weapons.’
’Gold isn’t an issue anymore, at least for now.’
’And I already possess combat power far beyond my actual realm.’
The more Luke thought about it, the more he realized just how much he had gained in a little over twenty days since arriving in Valtharion.
Back then...
He had been nothing.
An insignificant ant who could have been crushed by almost anyone.
Now, however.
He possessed enough strength to contend with the weakest among the world’s true powerhouses.
’Even so...’ Luke leaned back against the sofa.
’The truly high-level beings could still kill me without much difficulty.’
On the surface, he had the protection of the Holy Church. And the Saintess was also an previous hero of light, meaning few human forces would dare openly target him.
But Luke knew better than to believe that guaranteed his safety.
’Demon Whisper... demons... the other races... hidden assassins...’
One name after another surfaced in his mind.
The more he considered the threats lurking beyond the public eye.
The more he realized that his earlier confidence had been somewhat hollow.
Against ordinary enemies, he was undeniably powerful.
But against the beings truly standing at the peak of Valtharion.
He was still far from strong enough. So all his strength now seems like fake.
A single Platinum Knight. That was all it would take.
Someone at that level could kill him before he even realized what had happened.
With that thought, Luke leaned forward once more and looked at Jasper with renewed interest.
"And how exactly does the Silver Exchange intend to invest in me?"
Jasper smiled, as though he had been expecting that question.
"Within our capabilities, Baron Luke, we can provide almost any resource."
"Gold, Rare elixirs, Secret techniques, Ascension Series, Artifacts."
"Even soldiers, if necessary."
Luke listened quietly.
The more Jasper listed the benefits, the more convinced he became that his initial assumption had been correct.
Everything being offered was certainly valuable. But none of it addressed what he actually lacked.
After a brief pause, Luke shook his head.
"Manager Jasper..."
"I appreciate the offer, but I don’t have a need for those things."
Jasper was visibly surprised by Luke’s response.
A moment later, however, a look of realization crossed his face.
’The gifts from those wealthy merchant houses.’
’And perhaps the Holy Church has been supporting the Hero all this time as well.’
The more he thought about it, the more convinced he became.
If that were true, then it wasn’t strange that Baron Luke lacked neither wealth nor resources.
But that left Jasper with a difficult problem.
’Then... what exactly can the Silver Exchange offer him?’
He fell silent, carefully considering every possibility.
Unfortunately, nothing came to mind.
They didn’t possess forbidden techniques.
Nor did they have legendary treasures such as high-rank Origin Fruits.
The greatest strength of a merchant family had always been its vast fortune and access to resources.
Yet, for the first time in many years...
Jasper felt that those very strengths held surprisingly little value in front of the young Hero.
So he looked directly at Luke before speaking with complete sincerity.
"Then allow me to ask you instead, Baron Luke."
"Is there anything you truly need?
"If it is within the Silver Exchange’s capabilities, we will do everything we can to provide it."
Luke fell silent.
His eyebrows drew together as he carefully considered the question.
Instead of thinking about wealth or treasures.
One name surfaced in his mind.
*The Demon Whisper.*
Their previous attempt in Stormveil County had ended in failure.
But who could guarantee they wouldn’t strike again?
’What if next time they send a Platinum Knight Or even a Diamond Knight...?’
Against opponents of that level, he wouldn’t stand a chance.
Worse still-
Their objective might not even be limited to kidnapping him.
They could simply slaughter everyone standing in their way.
As images of Aurielle’s smile, Aurora’s cheerful face, and the others flashed through his mind, Luke slowly came to a realization.
Blackstone still wasn’t safe enough.
’Even in the worst-case scenario. I might be able to escape with my Titan abilities.’
’But they can’t.’
Luke’s expression turned grim.
Of course, that was assuming he even had the chance to flee.
If a true powerhouse appeared without warning, survival itself would be uncertain.
After a long silence, Luke leaned forward.
The smile on his face had completely disappeared.
Looking Jasper straight in the eyes, he calmly stated the one thing he truly needed.
"I need..."
"A Diamond-rank powerhouse stationed in Blackstone Territory."
That was the most practical solution he could think of.
If the enemy sent an overwhelming expert. Then only another overwhelming expert could stop them.
Even if that person couldn’t win, buying a little time would be enough.
Enough time for Luke to gather everyone...
And escape.
But it seems he thought Diamond ranks are cabbages who could be found anywhere.
"What?!"
Jasper shot to his feet, his eyes wide with disbelief.
Luke blinked in confusion.
’Brather? why are you reacting like that?’
’You’re acting as if I just asked for your daughter’s hand in marriage.’
If Jasper could somehow hear those thoughts...
He would probably agree to the marriage without much hesitation.
But a Diamond-rank powerhouse?
That was another matter entirely.
After several moments, Jasper finally composed himself.
Taking a slow, deep breath, he eased back into his seat before looking at Luke with an unusually serious expression.
"Baron Luke..."
"Do you truly understand what a Diamond-rank powerhouse represents?"
There wasn’t the slightest trace of mockery in his voice.
He was asking a genuine question.

chapters.title: Chapter 216: The Secret Behind a Platinum Knight
paragraphs: "Sir Luke, Diamond Rank beings are existences whose mere presence is enough to threaten an entire Kingdom."
Luke’s expression froze.
A kingdom.
In terms of sheer territory, it was already comparable to—if not even larger than—the countries of his previous world.
Yet Jasper was saying.
A single Diamond Knight could threaten such a force?
Seeing Luke’s disbelief, Jasper smiled bitterly and slowly shook his head.
"Our family has only one Early Diamond Knight."
"And for the past five hundred years..."
"Not a single additional Diamond Knight has been born within our house."
His voice was calm, but the hint of regret hidden within it was impossible to miss.
He didn’t mention the most important fact.
The only reason his family had survived, expanded, and eventually grown into the commercial giant it was today.
Was because that lone Diamond Knight still stood behind them.
Without that supreme powerhouse. Their unimaginable wealth would have become a curse rather than a blessing.
Sooner or later, powerful enemies would have united, launched a full-scale war against them, and seized everything the family had spent centuries building.
In this world.
Wealth alone could never guarantee survival.
Only overwhelming strength could truly protect it.
There’s another reason. Diamond Rank beings are incredibly difficult to kill.
Especially by someone below their own realm. Those beneath the Diamond Rank can hardly even hope to injure one.
But he also didn’t mention this to Luke.
Luke fell silent.
This revelation stunned him even more than the previous one.
Five hundred years. And only a single Diamond Knight?
The thought sent a chill through his heart.
What made it even harder to believe was the identity of Jasper’s family.
They were one of the continent’s greatest merchant unions memebers, possessing huge wealth and access to rare resources. If anyone had the means to nurture powerful experts, it should have been them.
Yet. Even with mountains of resources and with the guidance of an existing Diamond Knight in those five centuries.
They still hadn’t produced a second one.
That fact alone spoke volumes.
It showed just how impossibly rare Diamond Rank powerhouses truly were.
At that moment, Luke realized he had gravely underestimated them.
Earlier, after learning that the Demon Whisper organization possessed Diamond Knights and that Count Magnus himself was one.
He had subconsciously begun treating the realm as something merely difficult to reach.
Now he understood how wrong that assumption had been.
While he didn’t knew, that Magnus hadn’t remained a Count because he lacked the strength to rise higher.
Quite the opposite.
With his cultivation alone, he already possessed the qualifications to contend for the title of Duke.
After all...
Even among the great Ducal Houses, the strongest experts were generally only Peak Diamond Knights.
The title of Count, was far from representing Magnus’s true standing.
Then Jasper’s voice pulled Luke out of his thoughts.
"Even though we can’t bring a Diamond Rank powerhouse..."
He stopped mid-sentence.
Silence filled the room as he looked directly into Luke’s eyes.
Luke met his gaze, waiting patiently for him to continue.
After a brief pause, Jasper spoke.
"I can bring a Platinum Rank powerhouse here." The words landed heavily.
Luke’s eyes narrowed slightly.
He immediately noticed the wording.
Jasper had said "I can," not "we can."
That small difference revealed a great deal.
In reality, Jasper already knew his family would never unanimously approve such a proposal.
After all...
Platinum Knights weren’t also cabbages growing by the roadside.
Even an organization of their size possessed only a handful of them.
Dispatching one to a newly established territory like Blackstone would inevitably face fierce opposition from the higher-ups.
But Jasper chose not to mention any of that.
Instead...
He made the decision himself.
Ever since arriving in Blackstone, everything he had witnessed had exceeded his expectations.
The territory expanded at an unbelievable pace.
Trade flourished day after day.
The mysterious Earth Mage. The inexplicable city walls.
And most importantly those Berserk Greatswordsmen.
Warriors who possessed abilities resembling bloodlines, to found here.
None of it made sense.
Yet all of it had happened under Hero Luke’s rule.
Jasper had long since realized that this young hero possessed far more secrets than anyone imagined.
So...
He decided to gamble.
Not on Blackstone.
But on Luke himself.
’I only hope, When Hero Luke truly rises to stand at the continent’s peak.’
’He won’t forget the people who chose to stand beside him while he was still climbing.’
Jasper let out a long sigh and leaned back against the sofa.
It seemed the difficult part was only beginning.
He would have to convince his mother.
She herself was a Platinum Knight, but Jasper already knew there was almost no chance she would agree to leave the family’s headquarters and come to Blackstone.
So...
His only realistic option was to persuade her to let his grandfather make the trip instead.
If anyone had a chance of accepting this proposal.
It was him.
Across the table, Luke quietly raised an eyebrow.
After Jasper’s earlier explanation, he had assumed that even dispatching a lower-ranked powerhouse would be nearly impossible.
After all...
If Diamond Knights were so unimaginably rare, then Platinum Knights couldn’t be common either.
Yet Jasper had voluntarily offered to bring one.
That was enough to pique Luke’s interest.
Something is better than nothing.
He silently weighed the advantages and disadvantages before relaxing back into the sofa once more.
For the foreseeable future. He had no confidence in closing the gap between himself and a Platinum Knight.
Not anytime soon.
Patrick had once shared a few stories about his father, who was a Platinum Knight.
Those brief descriptions alone had been enough for Luke to realize how terrifying that realm truly was.
In fact...
Despite being his own father, Patrick had rarely even met him.
Powerhouses of that level spent most of their lives cultivating, exploring ruins, or pursuing opportunities to advance further.
Remaining in one place for long periods was exceedingly rare.
That alone was enough to show just how distant the Platinum Rank was from ordinary cultivators.
Luke couldn’t help recalling the conversation he had once had with Patrick.
At the time, Patrick had simply repeated the words of his father.
"Patrick..."
"If hundreds of Silver Knights combine their strength, they can stall or even kill an Early Golden Knight."
Patrick had understood that much.
After all, quantity could sometimes overcome quality.
But Patrick’s expression had turned unusually solemn as he continued.
"However..."
"Even if hundreds of Peak Golden Knights attacked a single Early Platinum Knight..."
"They would all die the moment the Platinum Knight used the power that belongs exclusively to their realm."
Patrick still vividly remembered the shock he had felt upon hearing those words.
Patrick’s father had continued in the same calm tone.
"Once someone reaches the Platinum Rank."
"It’s no longer about how much Aether you possess."
"Nor is it about raw physical strength."
"To a Platinum Knight..."
"Every realm below them is nothing more than moths flying into a flame."
Those words had completely overturned Luke’s understanding of power.
If overwhelming numbers. Vast reserves of Aether and superior physical strength.
None of those could bridge the gap.
Then what exactly separated a Platinum Knight from everyone beneath them?
Unfortunately.
Patrick hadn’t known the answer either.
Or perhaps...
His father simply hadn’t told him.
Luke had remained puzzled ever since.
"Sir Luke?"
Jasper’s voice brought him back to reality.
"So, do you agree?"
Luke looked at Jasper for a brief moment before giving a firm nod.
"I agree."
