That fact alone spoke volumes.
It showed just how impossibly rare Diamond Rank powerhouses truly were.
At that moment, Luke realized he had gravely underestimated them.
Earlier, after learning that the Demon Whisper organization possessed Diamond Knights and that Count Magnus himself was one.
He had subconsciously begun treating the realm as something merely difficult to reach.
Now he understood how wrong that assumption had been.
While he didn’t knew, that Magnus hadn’t remained a Count because he lacked the strength to rise higher.
Quite the opposite.
With his cultivation alone, he already possessed the qualifications to contend for the title of Duke.
After all...
Even among the great Ducal Houses, the strongest experts were generally only Peak Diamond Knights.
The title of Count, was far from representing Magnus’s true standing.
Then Jasper’s voice pulled Luke out of his thoughts.
"Even though we can’t bring a Diamond Rank powerhouse..."
He stopped mid-sentence.
Silence filled the room as he looked directly into Luke’s eyes.
Luke met his gaze, waiting patiently for him to continue.
After a brief pause, Jasper spoke.
"I can bring a Platinum Rank powerhouse here." The words landed heavily.
Luke’s eyes narrowed slightly.
He immediately noticed the wording.
Jasper had said "I can," not "we can."
That small difference revealed a great deal.
In reality, Jasper already knew his family would never unanimously approve such a proposal.
After all...
Platinum Knights weren’t also cabbages growing by the roadside.
Even an organization of their size possessed only a handful of them.
Dispatching one to a newly established territory like Blackstone would inevitably face fierce opposition from the higher-ups.
But Jasper chose not to mention any of that.
Instead...
He made the decision himself.
Ever since arriving in Blackstone, everything he had witnessed had exceeded his expectations.
The territory expanded at an unbelievable pace.
Trade flourished day after day.
The mysterious Earth Mage.
The inexplicable city walls.
And most importantly those Berserk Greatswordsmen.
Warriors who possessed abilities resembling bloodlines, to found here.
None of it made sense.
Yet all of it had happened under Hero Luke’s rule.
Jasper had long since realized that this young hero possessed far more secrets than anyone imagined.
So...
He decided to gamble.
Not on Blackstone.
But on Luke himself.
’I only hope, When Hero Luke truly rises to stand at the continent’s peak.’
’He won’t forget the people who chose to stand beside him while he was still climbing.’
Jasper let out a long sigh and leaned back against the sofa.
It seemed the difficult part was only beginning.
He would have to convince his mother.
She herself was a Platinum Knight, but Jasper already knew there was almost no chance she would agree to leave the family’s headquarters and come to Blackstone.
So...
His only realistic option was to persuade her to let his grandfather make the trip instead.
If anyone had a chance of accepting this proposal.
It was him.
Across the table, Luke quietly raised an eyebrow.
After Jasper’s earlier explanation, he had assumed that even dispatching a lower-ranked powerhouse would be nearly impossible.
After all...
If Diamond Knights were so unimaginably rare, then Platinum Knights couldn’t be common either.
Yet Jasper had voluntarily offered to bring one.
That was enough to pique Luke’s interest.
Something is better than nothing.
He silently weighed the advantages and disadvantages before relaxing back into the sofa once more.
For the foreseeable future.
He had no confidence in closing the gap between himself and a Platinum Knight.
Not anytime soon.
Patrick had once shared a few stories about his father, who was a Platinum Knight.
Those brief descriptions alone had been enough for Luke to realize how terrifying that realm truly was.
In fact...
Despite being his own father, Patrick had rarely even met him.
Powerhouses of that level spent most of their lives cultivating, exploring ruins, or pursuing opportunities to advance further.
Remaining in one place for long periods was exceedingly rare.
That alone was enough to show just how distant the Platinum Rank was from ordinary cultivators.
Luke couldn’t help recalling the conversation he had once had with Patrick.
At the time, Patrick had simply repeated the words of his father.
"Patrick..."
"If hundreds of Silver Knights combine their strength, they can stall or even kill an Early Golden Knight."
Patrick had understood that much.
After all, quantity could sometimes overcome quality.
But Patrick’s expression had turned unusually solemn as he continued.
"However..."
"Even if hundreds of Peak Golden Knights attacked a single Early Platinum Knight..."
"They would all die the moment the Platinum Knight used the power that belongs exclusively to their realm."
Patrick still vividly remembered the shock he had felt upon hearing those words.
Patrick’s father had continued in the same calm tone.
"Once someone reaches the Platinum Rank."
"It’s no longer about how much Aether you possess."
"Nor is it about raw physical strength."
"To a Platinum Knight..."
"Every realm below them is nothing more than moths flying into a flame."
Those words had completely overturned Luke’s understanding of power.
If overwhelming numbers.
Vast reserves of Aether and superior physical strength.
None of those could bridge the gap.
Then what exactly separated a Platinum Knight from everyone beneath them?
Unfortunately.
Patrick hadn’t known the answer either.
Or perhaps...
His father simply hadn’t told him.
Luke had remained puzzled ever since.
"Sir Luke?"
Jasper’s voice brought him back to reality.
"So, do you agree?"
Luke looked at Jasper for a brief moment before giving a firm nod.
"I agree."

chapters.title: Chapter 217: Selene, Luke Second Wife Is Coming
paragraphs: There was no reason to refuse.
Whether for himself Or for Blackstone.
Having a Platinum Knight guarding the territory would bring benefits that far outweighed any potential drawbacks.
"Of course." Luke added another condition.
"The Platinum Knight’s presence must remain a secret."
"At the very least, it cannot be made public."
Jasper nodded without hesitation.
"That’s fine."
As hidden guardian was, in many ways, even more valuable than one whose existence was known to everyone.
Jasper smiled faintly.
"My grandfather prefers it that way as well."
With that matter settled, Luke stood up, preparing to leave.
Just as he about to completly stood up...
Jasper spoke again. "Sir Luke."
Luke stopped and sit down again.
"My eldest daughter, Isaria, is currently a professor at Horizon Astralis Academy."
"You should meet her."
A trace of fatherly pride appeared on Jasper’s face.
"She is a remarkably intelligent woman."
"I’m certain you’ll appreciate her personality."
Luke maintained a polite smile.
Inside, however.
’Another matchmaking attempt.’ The thought surfaced almost instantly.
Ever since his identity as a Hero had spread, people seemed strangely enthusiastic about introducing him to their daughters.
Still.
Another question quickly replaced that thought.
’Horizon Astralis Academy?’
’What kind of place is that?’
’And... why he was talking, like I am going there?’
Seeing the confusion on Luke’s face, Jasper blinked in surprise.
He frowned slightly before asking,
"Sir Luke, has Lady Selene not sent you her invitation?"
Luke’s confusion only deepened.
"Why would Selene send me an invitation?"
"And even if she did. Wouldn’t it be from Empyrean Academy?"
Jasper looked at him for a moment before realizing that Luke genuinely knew nothing about it.
"I see..."
Then he began explaining.
"Recently, Empyrean Academy decided to hold an academic exchange at Horizon Astralis Academy, located in the Eldric Sunborn Kingdom, which is the kingdom, currently we are residing."
"It will be a gathering where professors and scholars from numerous academies across the continent will meet with the professors of Empyrean Academy."
"The purpose is to exchange knowledge, discuss magical research, and strengthen academic ties."
He paused before adding,
"And Miss Selene will be attending as one of Empyrean Academy’s representatives."
Luke’s pupils contracted.
’Selene? She’s coming to the Human Continent?’
’And to the very same kingdom I’m in?’
For a brief moment, his thoughts came to a complete stop.
It had been so long since they last met.
Without realizing it, memories of her playful smile, teasing voice, and cheerful laughter surfaced one after another.
A faint smile almost appeared on his face.
Then confusion replaced it.
’Why didn’t I know about this?’
Jasper had already mentioned an invitation several times.
Yet no matter how hard Luke searched his memory. He couldn’t recall receiving anything during the past week.
Seeing the bewilderment on Luke’s face, Jasper continued.
"The exchange is scheduled for the first day of the Month of Fructus."
"That is..."
"Twenty days from now."
Those words echoed in Luke’s mind.
Only twenty days remained before Selene would arrive in the Eldric Sunborn Kingdom.
And somehow, he hadn’t heard a single thing about it.
Jasper spoke once more, pulling Luke out of his thoughts.
"Sir, I also confirmed that the letter from Empyrean Academy was delivered to Blackstone."
"It may still be somewhere inside your mansion."
Luke nodded absentmindedly.
His mind was already racing.
’If it reached the territory. Then where did it go?’
He quickly eliminated one possibility after another.
No one in Blackstone Manor would dare steal something addressed to him.
Especially a letter bearing the seal of Empyrean Academy.
Then...
A single name surfaced in his mind.
Luke’s eyebrow twitched.
’Aurielle.’
There was probably only one person in the entire mansion bold enough to "temporarily keep" a letter meant for him.
And somehow, the more he thought about it. The more believable that possibility became.
"Alright, Sir Jasper." Luke stood up and gave him a courteous nod.
"I’ll take my leave."
"Safe travels, Sir Luke."
Just as Luke was about to walk out of the room.
Jasper suddenly remembered something.
"Oh, right."
He took out a small metallic card from his spatial ring and handed it over.
"This contains my eldest daughter’s information."
"If you ever visit Horizon Astralis Academy."
"You can use it to find Isaria."
Luke accepted the metal card with a nod before storing it inside his spatial ring.
Only then did he leave the room.
At this moment, there was only one thing on his mind.
’Aurielle, where did you hide that invitation?’
Jasper walked to the window and watched Luke’s figure gradually disappear toward Blackstone Manor.
A faint smile appeared on his aged face.
"I just hope Isaria will like Sir Luke."
He muttered those words under his breath before letting out a helpless sigh.
Among all his children.
The one who worried him the most was his eldest daughter.
Not because of her talent.
Nor because of her career.
In fact, she excelled in both.
As one of the youngest professors at Horizon Astralis Academy, her future was already brighter than that of countless nobles.
The real problem was her marriage.
No matter how many outstanding young men were introduced to her. She rejected every single one of them.
Her answer never changed.
"I’m not interested."
At first, Jasper thought it was because none of the candidates met her standards.
But after years passed. He finally realized the truth.
His daughter simply had no interest in marriage at all.
That alone gave him endless headaches.
So, when he met Luke. An extraordinary Hero with limitless potential.
He couldn’t help but hope that, perhaps...
For the first time, his daughter might show even the slightest interest.
A few moments later, Luke finally returned to the mansion before making his way toward the Time Chamber.
Soon, he arrived in front of the cozy bungalow that served as their home.
"Huff..." He let out a long breath, trying to steady himself.
’Why am I this nervous?’
Shaking his head, he reached for the door.
Creak.
The wooden door slowly opened. Luke stepped inside the bedroom.

Aurielle was sitting quietly before the dressing mirror, gently combing her long black hair. Fresh droplets of water still clung to the silky strands, occasionally sliding down onto her shoulders. It was obvious she had only recently finished bathing.
She wore her usual purple nightgown—the one she only ever wore inside the house.
The room was silent.
Only the soft sound of the comb gliding through her hair echoed faintly.
Aurielle didn’t turn around. She simply continued combing her hair as though she hadn’t noticed Luke’s arrival.
Luke, however, knew better.
She definitely noticed. She’s just pretending she didn’t.
For some inexplicable reason his heartbeat sped up.
’Why do I suddenly feel like an employee walking into his boss’s office to ask for a salary raise?’
The absurd comparison popped into his mind, making the corner of his mouth twitch.
Taking another quiet breath. Luke cautiously walked into the room.
Step by step, he approached Aurielle, who was quietly humming to herself as she continued combing her damp hair.
"La~ la~ la~"
Her gentle voice filled the room, as soothing as ever.
Without even turning around, the corners of her lips curved into a soft smile.
Luke caught the reflection of that smile in the mirror.
"My darling is back."
Her tone was light and cheerful.
"What happened?"
"You came home unusually early today."
She asked casually, still combing her long black hair.
Normally, Luke spent most of his time inspecting Blackstone and patrolling its surroundings, rarely returning before late at night.
Today he had come back much earlier than usual.
"Nothing." Luke smiled warmly.
"I just missed you."
Closing the remaining distance, he wrapped his arms around her slender waist from behind.

chapters.title: Chapter 218: Aurielle’s Love Evolved
paragraphs: Aurielle’s hand paused for the briefest moment.
Then her smile deepened.
The comb slowly came to a stop as she leaned back slightly into his embrace, enjoying the familiar warmth.
"So, You finally remembered your wife?"
A teasing smile appeared on her face, though the happiness hidden in her eyes was impossible to conceal.
Aurielle didn’t think much of the hug.
After all, they had spent almost the entire previous night together, makinglove, so Luke suddenly acting affectionate again was a little unusual.
But she didn’t mind.
In fact she rather liked it.
Seeing that she seemed to be in a good mood, Luke rested his chin lightly on her shoulder and met her eyes through the mirror.
Keeping his expression as natural as possible, he asked in an almost casual tone,
"Honey."
"Did you happen to receive an invitation letter from Empyrean Academy?"
His voice was calm.
Too calm.
He deliberately avoided sounding suspicious or accusatory, asking as though it were nothing more than an ordinary question.
Yet.
The moment those words left his mouth—
Aurielle’s hand stopped. The comb froze halfway through her hair.
Even the gentle smile reflected in the mirror slowly disappeared.
The atmosphere inside the room changed almost instantly.
Luke felt his throat go dry.
’...Please don’t get angry.’
A long silence followed. Neither of them spoke.
Only after several moments did Aurielle resume combing her hair.
Stroke after stroke. Her movements remained graceful.
Her expression, however. Had become completely indifferent.
"Yes."
"I received it."
Her voice was calm. far too calm.
"And I burned it."
There wasn’t the slightest trace of a smile on her face anymore.
Only an icy stillness remained.
Aurielle’s expression remained completely unchanged.
There wasn’t the slightest hint of guilt on her face.
If anything, she looked as though she had merely done what any devoted wife should have done.
Luke: ’0-0’
The system: [0-0]
Luke’s eyebrow twitched.
’Huh?’
’Why are you making that face?’
He couldn’t understand the system’s reaction.
This was clearly a matter involving his second wife.
Yet this time. It had suddenly joined in with that strange expression.
Before Luke could complain any further.
A new notification appeared before his eyes.
[Natal Obsessive Love has successfully evolved.]
Luke’s pupils narrowed slightly.
His expression, however, remained perfectly calm.
He silently waited for the rest of the message.
Another panel appeared.
[Please fulfill the second condition to unlock the Second Milestone.]
[Target: Wife — Aurielle Valmont]
[Current Realm: Early Silver Knight]
[Status: Not Achieved.]
Luke stared blankly at the floating screen.
Then the corner of his mouth twitched.
’The hell? There was a second condition?’
’System! You never mentioned this before!’
He immediately began cursing the system in his mind.
The requirement had appeared completely out of nowhere.
[Luke, that’s a built-in safety measure.]
[Some users reached the peak, only to find themselves completely alone.]
[They happily accepted rewards from their wives but rarely invested those rewards back into them.]
[In the end, their wives died from accidents, battles... or simply old age.]
Luke’s expression stiffened.
’Just how many users has this system had before me?’ That question quietly surfaced in his mind.
Even so, his hand never stopped moving.
He continued gently running his fingers through Aurielle’s long, silky hair while silently conversing with the system.
Aurielle noticed the brief pause.
Her emerald eyes flickered with curiosity through the mirror.
But she didn’t interrupt him.
Instead, she quietly continued combing her hair.
Luke answered the system in his mind.
’Even if you hadn’t told me. I was always planning to help my wives become stronger.’
The system’s response came almost immediately.
[Sure, sure.]
Luke chose to ignore the obvious sarcasm.
Taking a quiet breath, he focused his attention entirely on Aurielle again.
Lowering his head slightly, he moved closer until their faces were reflected side by side in the mirror.
"Honey." His voice was gentle.
"Why did you do that?" He searched her eyes for an answer.
"What if. It contained something important for me?"
Aurielle’s lips twitched slightly.
’He still has the nerve to act innocent. Did he really think she didn’t know why he was asking?’
Taking a slow breath, she answered in what she believed was a perfectly normal tone.
Unfortunately.
To Luke, it sounded colder than the depths of winter.
"Don’t act so innocent in front of me."
Her fingers slowly tightened around the hand resting on her waist.
Not enough to hurt him. But enough to make her displeasure unmistakably clear.
"I know you want to meet Selene."
The instant she spoke Selene’s name. She slowly turned her head.
Their eyes met.
A sharp glare shot straight at Luke through the mirror.
It was enough to make even him instinctively stiffen.
Aurielle had accepted the existence of Luke’s other wives.
She truly had.
But acceptance, didn’t mean approval of everything he did.
Nor did it mean she would simply stand aside while her husband wandered wherever he pleased like an untethered bull.
After all...
Luke hadn’t earned his reputation as a womanizer for no reason.
Whether he realized it or not. Whenever they toured Blackstone together, Aurielle noticed everything.
Every lingering glance. Every blushing young woman.
Every noble lady who secretly stole another look at him.
Every adventurer who whispered to her companions after Luke walked past.
He remained blissfully unaware.
Aurielle, however saw every single one of them.
Every single one of those women looked at Luke with unmistakable longing.
That was the part Aurielle couldn’t understand.
She could accept the gazes of the female summons Luke had brought into the territory.
After all, he was their master.
Their admiration was only natural. But those other bit*hes.
Why were they looking at him like that?
Like they didn’t had any men in their own families.
Or had every decent man in Blackstone suddenly vanished, forcing them to stare so shamelessly at someone else’s husband?
The more Aurielle thought about it. The more annoyed she became.
Unfortunately.
Even now, she couldn’t find an answer.
Meanwhile, Luke quietly listened to her words.
He couldn’t deny them. She was right.
The moment he heard that Selene would soon arrive on the Human Continent.
His heart had genuinely raced with excitement.
He had missed her. Far more than he had realized.
Just the thought of seeing her again after so long made him unable to remain calm.
Even Luke himself couldn’t explain why.
Why did he feel so eager?
Why did simply hearing her name stir his emotions so deeply?
He didn’t know.
Just then, Aurielle spoke again.
This time the icy edge in her voice had disappeared.
In its place there was only worry and concern.
"And, Luke you haven’t forgotten the Demon Whisper plan? have you??"
The moment those words reached his ears. Luke’s expression became serious.
She had touched upon the greatest threat hanging over his head.
The enemy he feared the most.
Even though Jasper had promised to bring a Platinum Knight to Blackstone.
Luke still couldn’t allow himself to relax.
That promise protected the territory.
It didn’t guarantee his own safety once he stepped outside it.
Aurielle continued softly,
"If you leave Blackstone and travel that far. Your life will be in danger."
Her voice slowed as she turned around to face him completely.
Their eyes met. "I don’t want that."
There was no anger left. No jealousy. Only genuine concern.
After holding his gaze for several seconds, Aurielle quietly turned back toward the mirror.
The comb once again slid through her silky black hair.
Stroke after stroke.
Her final words were calm.
"So, there’s no need to go to Horizon Astralis."
Silence settled over the room.

Before Luke could complain any further.
A new notification appeared before his eyes.
[Natal Obsessive Love has successfully evolved.]
Luke’s pupils narrowed slightly.
His expression, however, remained perfectly calm.
He silently waited for the rest of the message.
Another panel appeared.
[Please fulfill the second condition to unlock the Second Milestone.]
[Target: Wife — Aurielle Valmont]
[Current Realm: Early Silver Knight]
[Status: Not Achieved.]
Luke stared blankly at the floating screen.
Then the corner of his mouth twitched.
’The hell?
There was a second condition?’
’System!
You never mentioned this before!’
He immediately began cursing the system in his mind.
The requirement had appeared completely out of nowhere.
[Luke, that’s a built-in safety measure.]
[Some users reached the peak, only to find themselves completely alone.]
[They happily accepted rewards from their wives but rarely invested those rewards back into them.]
[In the end, their wives died from accidents, battles... or simply old age.]
Luke’s expression stiffened.
’Just how many users has this system had before me?’ That question quietly surfaced in his mind.
Even so, his hand never stopped moving.
He continued gently running his fingers through Aurielle’s long, silky hair while silently conversing with the system.
Aurielle noticed the brief pause.
Her emerald eyes flickered with curiosity through the mirror.
But she didn’t interrupt him.
Instead, she quietly continued combing her hair.
Luke answered the system in his mind.
’Even if you hadn’t told me.
I was always planning to help my wives become stronger.’
The system’s response came almost immediately.
[Sure, sure.]
Luke chose to ignore the obvious sarcasm.
Taking a quiet breath, he focused his attention entirely on Aurielle again.
Lowering his head slightly, he moved closer until their faces were reflected side by side in the mirror.
"Honey." His voice was gentle.
"Why did you do that?" He searched her eyes for an answer.
"What if.
It contained something important for me?"
Aurielle’s lips twitched slightly.
’He still has the nerve to act innocent.
Did he really think she didn’t know why he was asking?’
Taking a slow breath, she answered in what she believed was a perfectly normal tone.
Unfortunately.
To Luke, it sounded colder than the depths of winter.
"Don’t act so innocent in front of me."
Her fingers slowly tightened around the hand resting on her waist.
Not enough to hurt him.
But enough to make her displeasure unmistakably clear.
"I know you want to meet Selene."
The instant she spoke Selene’s name.
She slowly turned her head.
Their eyes met.
A sharp glare shot straight at Luke through the mirror.
It was enough to make even him instinctively stiffen.
Aurielle had accepted the existence of Luke’s other wives.
She truly had.
But acceptance, didn’t mean approval of everything he did.
Nor did it mean she would simply stand aside while her husband wandered wherever he pleased like an untethered bull.
After all...
Luke hadn’t earned his reputation as a womanizer for no reason.
Whether he realized it or not.
Whenever they toured Blackstone together, Aurielle noticed everything.
Every lingering glance.
Every blushing young woman.
Every noble lady who secretly stole another look at him.
Every adventurer who whispered to her companions after Luke walked past.
He remained blissfully unaware.
Aurielle, however saw every single one of them.
Every single one of those women looked at Luke with unmistakable longing.
That was the part Aurielle couldn’t understand.
She could accept the gazes of the female summons Luke had brought into the territory.
After all, he was their master.
Their admiration was only natural.
But those other bit*hes.
Why were they looking at him like that?
Like they didn’t had any men in their own families.
Or had every decent man in Blackstone suddenly vanished, forcing them to stare so shamelessly at someone else’s husband?
The more Aurielle thought about it.
The more annoyed she became.
Unfortunately.
Even now, she couldn’t find an answer.
Meanwhile, Luke quietly listened to her words.
He couldn’t deny them.
She was right.
The moment he heard that Selene would soon arrive on the Human Continent.
His heart had genuinely raced with excitement.
He had missed her.
Far more than he had realized.
Just the thought of seeing her again after so long made him unable to remain calm.
Even Luke himself couldn’t explain why.
Why did he feel so eager?
Why did simply hearing her name stir his emotions so deeply?
He didn’t know.
Just then, Aurielle spoke again.
This time the icy edge in her voice had disappeared.
In its place there was only worry and concern.
"And, Luke you haven’t forgotten the Demon Whisper plan? have you??"
The moment those words reached his ears.
Luke’s expression became serious.
She had touched upon the greatest threat hanging over his head.
The enemy he feared the most.
Even though Jasper had promised to bring a Platinum Knight to Blackstone.
Luke still couldn’t allow himself to relax.
That promise protected the territory.
It didn’t guarantee his own safety once he stepped outside it.
Aurielle continued softly,
"If you leave Blackstone and travel that far.
Your life will be in danger."
Her voice slowed as she turned around to face him completely.
Their eyes met.
"I don’t want that."
There was no anger left.
No jealousy.
Only genuine concern.
After holding his gaze for several seconds, Aurielle quietly turned back toward the mirror.
The comb once again slid through her silky black hair.
Stroke after stroke.
Her final words were calm.
"So, there’s no need to go to Horizon Astralis."
Silence settled over the room.

chapters.title: Chapter 219: "I Love You, Luke." Her Final Words
paragraphs: Luke didn’t answer.
He simply continued gently running his fingers through her long hair.
Feeling his quiet response, Aurielle naturally assumed he had accepted her request.
The corners of her lips gradually lifted into a relieved smile.
Her heart, which had been tense since the beginning of the conversation, finally relaxed.
What she didn’t know, was that while his hand continued caressing her hair.
Luke’s mind had already begun thinking about something entirely different.
’System, are you absolutely certain my clone can remain active regardless of how far away I am?’
The reply came without the slightest hesitation.
[Yes.]
[Although your mastery over Shadow of Nyx is still at the abysmal level.]
[Even in its weakest state, the ability allows your clone to exist without any distance limitation.]
Luke’s eyes lit up. That was exactly the answer he had been hoping for.
The system continued.
[Furthermore...]
[Because of the Nexus Titan’s compatibility, transforming into another Titan Form will no longer automatically dispel your clone.]
A smile slowly spread across Luke’s face.
Perfect! that meant everything would work exactly as he had planned.
He could leave a clone behind in Blackstone to handle daily affairs and company with Aurielle.
While the real him quietly traveled alone to Horizon Astralis Academy in the capital of the Eldric Sunborn Kingdom.
Aurielle would remain worry free.
Blackstone would continue functioning as usual. And he could still meet Selene.
The more he thought about it. The wider his grin became.
’Kekeke.’
Luke laughed mischievously inside his mind.
The system immediately joined in.
[Kekeke.]
Luke replied without missing a beat.
’Kekeke.’
[Kekeke.]
For a brief moment...
One human and one system laughed together like two conspirators who had just devised the perfect plan.
Meanwhile...
Far away from the mansion, atop a tall tree hidden among the branches.
Two figures quietly observed everything through the open bedroom window.
Aurora tilted her head.
"Why is Master grinning like that?"
She stared at Luke’s suspicious smile before asking with complete innocence,
"It looks like he’s about to have an affair."
Vaelira’s lips twitched.
She slowly turned toward Aurora with a speechless expression.
"Where exactly did you learn something like that?"
Aurora blinked.
"Lucy told me." She answered as though it were the most obvious thing in the world.
"She said whenever a married man starts grinning to himself like that."
"It means he’s about to have an affair with another woman."
Vaelira silently covered her face with one hand.
’Lucy! what on earth are you teaching this innocent girl?’
After taking a deep breath, she patiently corrected her.
"Our Master isn’t that kind of person."
She spoke with absolute confidence.
Then a certain notebook flashed through her mind.
The one containing Luke’s ever-growing womanizer record.
The corner of her mouth twitched.
She coughed awkwardly before revising her statement.
"I mean. He doesn’t go chasing after random women."
Aurora nodded seriously.
"That’s true." After thinking about it for a moment, she reached the same conclusion.
Master wasn’t going after some stranger.
Though, they didn’t knew, that Luke was planning to meet his second wife.
So technically, Lucy was wrong.
If Luke had known the two of them were secretly watching from a distant tree.
He probably wouldn’t have been embarrassed by their conversation.
Instead. He would have stared at them with a completely speechless expression before asking,
"Don’t the two of you have any work to do?"
"Why do you always end up peeping on me?"
Unfortunately...
Luke remained blissfully unaware of their presence.
Ever since Vaelira and Aurora had broken through to the Golden Knight realm, they had become much more cautious.
Whenever they stalk Luke from the shadows, they deliberately kept a far greater distance than before.
At that range. Even with Luke’s enhanced senses.
He couldn’t detect them at all.
Meanwhile, the two women continued observing the bedroom from their hidden perch, completely convinced that their surveillance remained as flawless as ever.
"Honey." Luke took out a potion bottle and placed it gently into Aurielle’s hand. "Here.
It was a Bronze Knight Breakthrough Potion.
Strictly speaking. Aurielle no longer needed this to advance.
With her talent, she could complete the breakthrough on her own.
However, system rewards were different.
They were perfectly refined. Completely safe.
And beyond guaranteeing a flawless breakthrough, they also helped stabilize the user’s cultivation afterward.
There was simply no reason not to use it.
Aurielle looked down at the crystal vial before raising an eyebrow.
"Hm?" Then she accepted it under Luke’s unusually expectant gaze.
When she looked back up. He was still staring at her.
Almost as if he wanted her to drink it immediately.
Aurielle couldn’t help feeling slightly puzzled.
’Why is he in such a hurry?’
Still...
She didn’t ask. She trusted Luke completely.
If there was one thing she was absolutely certain of. It was that he would never do anything to harm her.
Without another word, she stood up and headed toward the training room beneath the house.
Luke quietly followed her there.
Soon.
Aurielle entered the cultivation chamber alone.
After sitting down cross-legged, she uncorked the vial and drank the potion in one smooth motion.
Luke remained outside the room, calmly waiting.
There wasn’t the slightest trace of anxiety on his face.
After all with a System-grade potion. The possibility of the breakthrough failing simply didn’t exist.
*He jinxed it.*
"System." Luke folded his arms as he waited outside the cultivation room.
"What exactly does this milestone reward?"
His voice was filled with anticipation.
The system answered almost immediately.
[A surprise is only enjoyable when it remains a surprise.]
Luke let out a helpless sigh.
’Of course. Why did I even bother asking?’
Just as he was about to give up. Another notification appeared.
[However...]
[This milestone grants far more than a simple increase in the Return Rate.]
"What?!"
Luke blurted it out so loudly that he immediately covered his own mouth.
Fortunately.
The cultivation room was soundproof enough, and Aurielle was deep in her breakthrough.
Otherwise, he might have disrupted her.
Still his curiosity instantly skyrocketed. If even the system described it that way.
Then the reward was definitely extraordinary.
Now oddly enough.
Luke seemed even more excited about Aurielle’s breakthrough than Aurielle herself.
Unable to stay still, he began pacing back and forth outside the room.
One lap.
Then another.
Then another.
He looked exactly like an anxious father waiting outside the delivery room for news of his first child.
Luke stopped mid-step.
’That’s a terrible analogy.’
He immediately shook the thought out of his head.
Meanwhile...
Inside the cultivation room. Aurielle had already consumed the breakthrough potion.
The medicinal energy spread rapidly through her body.
After enduring several minutes of intense pain. She could already sense herself approaching the breakthrough.
Then—
"Huh?" A confused murmur escaped her lips.
Something unexpected had happened. Her S-Rank Origin suddenly stirred.
At the same time.
Her Royal bloodline began violently surging through her body, as though something buried deep within it had awakened.
It was trying...
To break free.
’Restrictions?’ Aurielle’s brows knitted together.
That single thought left her even more confused.
’Restrictions? What restrictions?’
Before she could think any further—
Another wave of agony struck.
The pain intensified with every passing second. Her thoughts became sluggish.
She could barely maintain her concentration.
’It’s getting out of control...’
Panic flashed through her mind. She could clearly feel her bloodline and her Origin beginning to resonate with one another.
Not merely resonating. They were merging.
As though they were trying to awaken something that had remained dormant inside her since birth.
The pressure became unbearable.
Crack.
Tiny fissures suddenly appeared across her skin.
Then another.
And another.
Within moments, fine cracks spread across her arms, neck, and shoulders.
Yet. No blood flowed from them.
Instead. Dense shadow energy seeped out through every crack, slowly enveloping the entire cultivation room.
’Luke...’
The first person Aurielle thought of wasn’t herself.
It was him.
She instinctively worried that something might happen outside if this strange power continued to spread.
Then without any warning—
Her eyes changed.
The familiar color vanished.
In its place a brilliant radiance filled her pupils.
As though daylight itself had awakened within them.
The shadow energy leaking from Aurielle’s body suddenly came to an abrupt halt.
Then—
A completely different energy emerged.
From every crack across her body, brilliant daylight-colored energy began pouring out, replacing the darkness entirely.
"W-What?" Aurielle’s breathing became uneven.
She could no longer understand what was happening to her own body.
It was as if two completely opposite powers were fighting for dominance inside her.
Instinctively, she turned toward the cultivation room’s door.
Beyond it.
Luke was still patiently waiting, completely unaware of the terrifying transformation taking place inside.
For the first time in a long while. Fear gripped her heart.
Not because she feared death itself.
She still had unfinished promises.
She still had to rescue her mother.
She still had countless things left undone.
No.
That wasn’t the real reason. or only reason.
Aurielle smiled bitterly.
’I lied...’
’I’m simply afraid of leaving him.’
One memory after another surfaced before her eyes.
Luke’s carefree smile.
His embarrassed expression whenever she teased him.
His innocent face.
His determined gaze.
Every precious moment they had shared together.
She didn’t want those memories to become the last ones.
’Luke, I’m sorry...’
A gentle smile appeared on her lips.
By now the cracks had spread across her entire face.
Her whole body resembled a porcelain statue on the verge of collapse.
As countless glowing fissures covered every inch of her skin.
It looked as though. The slightest touch would cause her to shatter.
Then—
Her final thought echoed silently within her heart.
’I love you, Luke.’
BOOOOOOOOOOM—!!
A blinding explosion erupted from the cultivation room.
The entire bungalow vanished in an instant.
The terrifying pillar of radiant daylight burst upward, tearing through the house before continuing into the sky above.
The ground trembled violently.
The entire Time Chamber shook as if struck by a catastrophe.
A colossal pillar of brilliant light—
Over one hundred meters wide—
Shot toward the heavens, as though attempting to pierce the very sky of the Time Chamber itself.
Every person inside the Time Chamber froze.
Then—
Everyone horrified gazes turned toward the source of the explosion.
Where Luke and Aurielle’s home had once stood. Only that overwhelming pillar of daylight remained.
"MASTER!!!"
Aurora’s scream echoed across the Time Chamber.
"MY LADY!!!"
Margaret’s panicked cry followed immediately after.

chapters.title: Chapter 220: Luke Thought He Lost Her Forever
paragraphs: Earlier...
The instant the blinding explosion erupted—
Luke’s instincts roared.
For a fleeting moment. The entire world seemed to slow down.
Even the expanding wall of radiant energy appeared sluggish in his vision.
Although Luke wasn’t transformed into a Titan. His instincts had recently become far sharper than before.
They could now sense even the slightest hint of fatal danger.
Normally.
He would receive a warning long before an attack reached him.
Yet this time. They had completely failed.
Because Aurielle’s Shadow affinity naturally possessed concealment properties.
Perhaps, that very element had hidden the danger until the final instant.
Meanwhile, every instinct in his body screamed only one thing.
Protect yourself!
So without hesitation. Luke reached out with his will.
He didn’t try to choose a specific Titan.
Nor did he attempt a full transformation.
There simply wasn’t enough time.
Instead. He issued the fastest command possible.
Armor.
Any Titan Armor.
Just come!
The very next instant. Valzareth answered his call.
Dark-blue Void Armor instantly manifested around Luke’s body, covering him from head to toe in a fraction of a second.
At the same time.
Two other energies briefly flickered around him.
One was pure white.
The other radiated a faint cosmic glow.
Nullex.
Elythos.
Both Titan Armaments had responded as well. But they were not fast as Valzareth.
So, the moment Valzareth finished materializing. The other two quietly dispersed.
Only one Titan Armor could exist at a time.
Although everything seemed to unfold over several moments.
In reality. It all happened within a tiny fraction of a second.
That’s why, just before the explosion reached him. Luke was already completely encased within Valzareth.
Then—
BOOOOOOOOOOM!!!
The deafening blast finally arrived.
The explosion was so violent that, without Valzareth’s protection, the sound alone would have ruptured Luke’s eardrums.
Yet...
The next scene that followed completely defied reason.
The boundless pillar of radiant light engulfed Luke.
But, it never struck or burned him.
It didn’t even attempted to push him away.
Instead.
The dazzling light gently flowed around the Void Armor.
Like a loving breeze.
Like warm sunlight embracing someone precious.
It softly brushed against Valzareth’s armored surface.
Almost...
As though it was afraid of hurting him.
There wasn’t the slightest trace of hostility within the light.
Only warmth and affection.
It was as though, Harming Luke...
Was the very last thing this radiant power would ever choose to do.
Luke, however didn’t notice any of it.
As his survival instincts subsided and his thoughts caught up with reality—
His face turned deathly pale. His pupils shrank to pinpoints.
Thump! Thump! Thump!
His heartbeat pounded wildly against his chest, as though it wanted to burst free.
An overwhelming sense of dread swallowed him whole.
’Aurielle!’
Her name echoed through his mind like a desperate scream.
Only then did he remember.
Aurielle had been inside the cultivation room.
The explosion had come from there.
His mind went completely blank.
He didn’t question what had caused it. He didn’t even wonder why it had happened.
Nothing else mattered. Only one thought remained.
’Aurielle...’
’Where are you?!’
Luke’s head snapped from side to side.
His eyes desperately searched through the blinding light and scattered debris.
The cultivation room, The walls , The house. Everything had vanished.
Every passing second. The dread inside Luke’s heart grew heavier.
A terrifying premonition slowly crept into his mind.
One he refused to acknowledge.
’Nothing could have happened to her.’
’She’s fine.’
’She has to be fine.’
Clinging to that belief, Luke acted without hesitation.
’Nyx Ascension.’
Next instant, darkness erupted around him. His body rapidly expanded as black-blue armor spread across every inch of his figure.
Within moments.
A fourteen-foot-tall Luke-Nyx Titan stood amidst the shattered remains of the house.
Above his head, the Void Halo slowly rotated, pulsing with dense Void energy.
Without wasting a single heartbeat. Luke activated Crown of the Void.
Void perception instantly swept across everything within a fifty-meter radius.
Nothing could be found, No heartbeat, no aura , no sign of Aurielle.
His breathing became ragged.
"AURIELLE!!"
"WHERE ARE YOU?!"
His desperate roar echoed throughout the Time Chamber.
The only thing his senses detected, was the boundless radiant energy surrounding him.
It felt alive. Almost as if it possessed a will of its own.
Yet Luke ignored it completely.
His entire mind was consumed by a single objective.
Find Aurielle.
Then—
The system’s voice exploded inside his mind.
[Luke! CALM DOWN!]
The sudden shout struck him like a hammer.
Luke froze. His frantic movements also came to an abrupt halt.
But not the panic on his face.
His breathing was still uneven. And his eyes still desperately searched the ruins, refusing to give up.
Seeing his condition, the system spoke again.
[Focus on the Golden Chain.]
That was all it said.
Yet those four words struck Luke like a bolt of lightning.
’The Golden Chain, how could I forget?’
Without another thought, Luke immediately focused inward.
Toward his heart.
The next instant. Five radiant golden chains materialized before him.
Invisible to everyone else. Only Luke could see them.
Four of the chains stretched far into the distance, disappearing beyond the horizon.
His other wives.
Then—
His gaze locked onto the final chain.
It didn’t extend anywhere. It remained perfectly still.
Connected to the very place where he was standing.
Luke’s eyes widened.
"What?" He looked around in disbelief.
"But! there’s nothing here!" His frustrated shout echoed through the shattered surroundings.
The chain pointed directly toward the center of the radiant light.
The same place engulfed by that mysterious hundred-meter-wide field of daylight energy.
Yet...
There was nothing.
Nothing his eyes could recognize.
Just as confusion overwhelmed him—
The radiant field suddenly trembled.
A heartbeat later—
SHHHHIIIIIING—!!
A blinding surge of daylight exploded outward.
The brilliant radiance swept across the entire Time Chamber in an instant.
Everyone present instinctively shut their eyes.
The light was simply too dazzling to look at directly.
Except Luke.
Whether it was because of Valzareth or because the mysterious radiance refused to harm him. The blinding light had no effect on his vision.
He continued staring at its center. The panic consuming him slowly gave way to confusion.
’What is this light?’ But before he could think any further—
OHHHHHMMMMMM—!
A deep, resonance echoed throughout the entire Time Chamber.
The sound seemed to come from everywhere at once.
The next instant. The boundless sea of daylight began shrinking.
Streams of radiant energy converged from every direction.
They gathered, Condensed, Compressed.
Until all of it was concentrated at a single point directly before Luke.
Then—
A silhouette slowly emerged from within the light.
Luke’s eyes widened.
The shape gradually became clearer.
Which returned Life to his eyes.
"Aurielle." The whisper escaped his lips before he even realized it.
The radiant cocoon completely dissolved.
Aurielle stood there quietly.
Her long hair no longer shimmered with shades of black.
Instead it glowed with a soft daylight radiance. Her eyes had transformed as well.
Which now shown with Brilliant golden-white light.
The earlier explosion had reduced her clothes to nothing.
Her entire body was wrapped only in flowing strands of radiant light that naturally concealed her privite parts.
For a brief moment. Luke simply stood there.
Unable to believe she was truly alive.
Then—
"AURIELLE!"
Every ounce of panic vanished, replaced by overwhelming relief.

chapters.title: Chapter 221: The System’s Next Requirement... YANDERE?!
paragraphs: Without the slightest hesitation. He dismissed his Titan form.
Valzareth dissolved into particles of Void energy.
Luke returned to his human appearance and sprinted toward her with everything he had.
Then without saying a word. He pulled Aurielle tightly into his arms.
So tightly that it almost hurt.
Only when he felt the warmth of her body against his. Did the violent trembling running through him begin to ease.
His heartbeat gradually slowed.
And when he caught the familiar fragrance of lavender drifting from her hair.
Only then, did his shaking finally stop.
He buried his face against her shoulder, holding her as though he feared she would disappear again if he loosened his grip.
Aurielle quietly felt every bit of Luke emotions, the fear, the worry, the love.
The panic he had desperately tried to suppress.
All of it was contained within that embrace.
A wave of guilt washed over her heart.
She had never imagined her breakthrough would cause something like this.
Nor had she expected Luke to be frightened to such an extent.
Her arms slowly wrapped around his back.
"Luke..."
"I’m fine."
She gently rubbed his back, trying to reassure him.
"I’m really fine."
At the same time. Relief also filled her own heart.
She hadn’t lost him. She was still alive.
Which meant. She could continue spending her days with the man she loved.
Luke didn’t answer for a moment.
Instead his arms tightened around her even more.
As though he was silently confirming she was truly there.
Feeling the strength of his embrace. The guilt in Aurielle’s heart deepened further.
She lowered her head slightly until her lips rested beside his ear.
Then, in a barely audible whisper.
"I’m sorry for scaring you."
Hearing those words. Luke hugged her even tighter.
Without letting go, he replied in a slightly trembling voice,
"D-Don’t..." He swallowed hard.
"D-Don’t ever do that again."
He clearly wanted to sound angry. To scold her.
Yet the words came out as nothing more than a frightened stutter.
Aurielle couldn’t help smiling. Which brings a soft laugh from her lips.
She gently stroked his back before answering in a voice overflowing with affection.
"As my husband wishes~"
Silence returned. Neither of them spoke again.
They simply remained in each other’s embrace.
To anyone watching. It might have looked like they had forgotten the entire world.
Luke never asked what had caused the explosion. Or why it had happened.
From everything he knew. Nothing should have been capable of entering the Time Chamber without him noticing.
He had personally confirmed that fact during his long stay there.
So, the only thing that mattered to him right now was that Aurielle was alive.
Aurielle also chose not to explain anything. Not because she wanted to hide it.
But because she understood something.
No amount of words could reassure Luke more than this embrace.
As long as she remained in his arms. He would know she was safe.
That alone was enough. For now.
Though, the quiet moment between them didn’t last long.
"MASTER!!"
"MY LADY!!"
Still even after hearing all of them. Luke still didn’t loosen his embrace.
He simply continued holding Aurielle as though he never intended to let go again.
Aurielle smiled helplessly. Then she quietly whispered,
"Luke."
"You do realize. I’m currently naked."
Luke froze.
Only then did he remember.
In his panic...
He had completely forgotten that the explosion had destroyed all of Aurielle’s clothes.
"Ahem."
Without another word, he opened his System Space, took out a fresh set of magical clothes, and handed them to her.
"Here."
Aurielle accepted them with a gentle smile.
The moment she put them on. The enchanted fabric automatically adjusted itself to her figure.
Within seconds. It transformed into the familiar loose robe she usually wore inside the Time Chamber.
Aurielle lowered her eyes to examine it before smiling again.
"It still amazes me." She softly ran her fingers across the robe.
"These magical clothes can change into whatever I want every time."
Although she had already been wearing magical attire before the breakthrough.
She still found the craftsmanship fascinating.
After all.
Such clothing was incredibly expensive. Only skilled Artificers or high-ranking Mages could create items like these.
A few moments later. Everyone finally arrived.
Aurora was the first to rush over, followed closely by Vaelira, Margaret, Elena, and the others.
The moment they saw Luke and Aurielle standing there safely. Every one of them let out a long sigh of relief.
The overwhelming fear that had gripped their hearts finally disappeared.
"Elena." Luke looked toward her.
"Take care of Aurielle." The moment those words left his mouth.
Aurielle shot him an annoyed glare. She had already told him she was fine.
Yet he was still treating her as though she might collapse at any moment.
Luke pretended not to notice.
Because after what had just happened. He wasn’t willing to take even the slightest risk.
As for everything that had occurred during her breakthrough. That discussion could wait.
Right now...
He needed a little time alone. If he stayed beside Aurielle any longer. He knew he would never let go of her.
The fear lingering in his heart hadn’t completely faded yet.
His emotions were still in turmoil.
Elena immediately nodded.
"I understand, My Lord."
Without another word. Luke quietly turned around and walked away.
Meanwhile.
Aurora, Vaelira, Margaret, Elena, and everyone else gathered around Aurielle, asking one question after another.
"What happened?"
"Why did that explosion occur?"
"Are you injured anywhere?"
Aurielle answered them one by one while occasionally glancing toward Luke’s departing figure.
A few minutes later.
Luke was walking alone across the distant hills of the Time Chamber.
The surrounding wind quietly brushed past him.
Then, the system’s voice echoed inside his mind.
[Luke.]
[You need to be more careful when using the Time Chamber.]
[If the energy released during that breakthrough had been even slightly stronger...]
[The Time Chamber itself could have been destroyed.]
Luke remained silent. He had already realized it himself.
The explosion released during Aurielle’s breakthrough had possessed raw destructive power comparable to a peak Golden Knight.
That level of energy had actually damaged the Time Chamber.
Even now...
It was repairing itself by drawing mana from the Mana Well.
Luke let out a slow sigh. "I’ll have to upgrade them too."
The Time Chamber. The Mana Well. The Healing Spring.
All three required special blueprints from the System before they could be upgraded.
Unfortunately.
During the past seven days, not a single blueprint had appeared among his daily rewards.
Perhaps, his luck had simply been terrible lately.
Luke shook his head.
There was no point dwelling on it now. He could think about it another time.
Just then the system spoke again.
This time, its words instantly eased the lingering heaviness in Luke’s heart.
[Luke.]
[The next milestone has been reached.]
[Would you like to check it?]
Luke blinked.
Then he smacked his forehead.
"I completely forgot about that."
A smile finally appeared on his face. His earlier panic and worry subsided, replaced by curiosity and anticipation.
Without hesitation. He nodded.
"Show me."
The next moment a familiar notification appeared before his eyes.
[10,000× Return System Milestone Achieved.]
[1st : LOVE AND POSSESSIVENESS (✔)]
Benefits: 100x Base Multiplier.
[2nd : OBSESSIVE LOVE AND SILVER KNIGHT (✔)]
Benefits:
- 1,000x Base Multiplier.
- Stacking Daily Charges.
- Monthly Claim Limit: 2/1,000
[3rd : YANDERE ??? (✗)]

chapters.title: Chapter 222: "What the Heck Is a Healthy Yandere?!"
paragraphs: "That’s insane." Luke couldn’t help muttering to himself.
His eyes shone with excitement as he read through the milestone’s benefits.
One feature immediately caught his attention.
Daily charge stacking.
Until now.
Whenever a reward triggered the 10,000× Return, the additional 100× passive multiplier from Aurielle became almost meaningless.
After all compared to ten thousand. One hundred was practically nothing.
But now, those daily charges could be accumulated instead of being wasted.
A grin slowly spread across Luke’s face. "Now that’s actually useful."
He had barely finished celebrating—
When another notification suddenly appeared before him.
Luke’s smile instantly froze.
"What?" A bad premotion immediately rose inside him.
He instinctively took half a step back.
If the System had possessed a physical body.
Luke would have already put several meters of distance between them, as though avoiding a contagious plague.
Seeing his reaction. The System calmly continued.
[Luke.]
[A new update has been installed.]
Luke’s eyelid twitched.
For some reason. He had an extremely bad feeling about this.
"...Go on." He answered cautiously.
The System didn’t keep him waiting.
[The previous base multiplier has now become the new Return rate.]
[From this point onward...]
[Aurielle’s Return will be fixed at 1,000×.]
Luke stared at the notification for several seconds.
Then—
"THIS IS ABSURD!" His shout echoed across the empty hills.
He looked completely speechless.
"Other people’s systems receive updates that add new functions and increase rewards."
"But mine?"
"It keeps finding new ways to reduce them!"
Luke couldn’t help complaining.
Although, He had to admit.
The Second Milestone had indeed unlocked several incredible features.
Still, at this moment. He genuinely missed those cliché slave systems from the novels he had read on Earth.
The System immediately responded.
[(ಠ_ಠ) Tch.]
[I’m far superior to those slave systems from your novel world.]
Its tone sounded strangely offended. As if Luke had insulted its dignity.
Completely ignoring Luke’s aggrieved expression. It continued speaking.
[However...]
[There is another piece of good news.]
Luke raised an eyebrow.
He had already learned from experience.
Whenever the System said "good news". There was usually a catch somewhere.
Still.
He patiently listened.
[Aurielle has successfully advanced to the Silver Knight Realm.]
[Silver Knight corresponds to D-Rank.]
[Therefore from this point onward, every reward generated through Aurielle will be fixed at D-Rank.]
Hearing that Luke’s mood improved slightly.
At least he wouldn’t be receiving rocks as rewards anymore.
The System immediately interrupted his thoughts.
[There are plenty of D-Rank rocks.]
Upon this Luke’s mouth twitched, as the system was hell-bent on giving him rocks.
The System completely ignored his expression and continued.
[Also the daily charges are cumulative.]
[They are not multiplicative.]
Luke quietly listened. The System gave an example.
[For instance, after accumulating charges for ten days.]
[The stored Return becomes 10,000×.]
Luke nodded.
"That’s about what I expected."
There was no way his System would leave such an obvious loophole unpatched.
If stacking had been multiplicative. The numbers would have become absurd within a few weeks.
Then another notification appeared.
[The reward upgrade limit has been adjusted.]
[Maximum upgrade: B-Rank.]
Luke’s expression stiffened slightly.
The System continued mercilessly.
[The previous 100× Upgrade option has been removed.]
[The first upgrade of a reward will now consume a 1,000× Return.]
[Upgrading that same reward a second time will require a 10,000× Return.]
Seeing this, Luke finally gave up arguing.
He let out a long sigh.
"Even the 100× Upgrade option is gone. What else is there to say?"
Complaining clearly wasn’t going to change anything.
After calming down, he looked at the update again.
Then a faint smile returned to his face.
"There is atleast one good thing."
Previously, everything depended on luck.
Only when a 10,000× Return happened to appear could he upgrade the same reward twice.
If his luck was poor. He simply had to wait.
Now, however the rules were fixed.
As long as he patiently accumulated charges. He could reliably upgrade a reward all the way to B-Rank.
That meant. In roughly ten days, he could create a Platinum-rank asset whenever he wanted.
Luke slowly nodded.
"I can work with that."
Then his gaze then shifted toward the final reward listed in the milestone.
Monthly Claim.
The moment he read those two words. His anticipation skyrocketed.
If...
If it really worked the way he imagined. Then everything would change.
His thoughts instantly began racing.
’Several plans I’ve been putting off. All of them suddenly seemed possible.’
Just as his excitement reached its peak. The System finally began explaining.
[The Monthly Claim is a Choice Reward—]
"FINALLY!" Before the System could even finish explaining. Luke threw both hands into the air and shouted toward the sky.
"So the Goddess of Luck hasn’t abandoned me after all!"
The System was silent for a moment.
Then...
A single notification appeared.
[o_O]
[The Goddess of Luck had nothing to do with this.]
[It was this System that added the feature you were cursing a moment ago.]
Luke immediately cleared his throat.
"Ahem."
His expression changed at lightning speed.
He smiled warmly.
"My dear System. You’ve always been the best."
The System remained completely unmoved.
It simply gave him a thoroughly shameless look.
Then it continued its explanation.
[With the Monthly Claim. You may choose any reward once every month.]
Luke’s eyes lit up.
The System continued.
[The selected reward will always be generated at the same realm as Aurielle.]
[Current Rank: D-Rank.]
Luke clenched his fists.
This was far more valuable than relying on random luck. He could deliberately choose exactly what Blackstone needed.
The System wasn’t finished yet.
[One Monthly Claim is generated at the beginning of every month.]
[However.]
[As compensation for this update. One extra claim has already been granted to you.]
Luke’s smile widened even further.
Then—
The final notification appeared.
[This compensation has been provided because several benefits previously exclusive to Aurielle have now been removed and distributed across your other wives return as well.]
"Now." Luke slowly looked toward the System.
"What exactly did you remove this time?" His voice carried more resignation than anger.
By now he had already accepted that every major update came with hidden conditions.
The System answered immediately.
[First.]
[Milestones have now become mandatory for your other wives.]
Luke frowned.
The System continued.
[Previously.]
[Even without unlocking Milestones, wives could still trigger 10,000× Returns through sufficiently strong emotions or the awakening of new emotions.]
[That is no longer possible.]
Luke’s expression gradually stiffened.
[From now onward.]
[A wife without her First Milestone unlocked will only generate 1× G-Rank rewards.]
[Which is effectively... nothing.]
Luke silently rubbed his forehead.
The System wasn’t finished.
[Only after reaching the First Milestone, will her Return become 100×.]
[The reward cap will also increase to E-Rank.]
Another notification appeared.
[Even if that wife’s cultivation surpasses the reward limit. Higher-ranked rewards will not be generated.]
[To unlock them. Complete their Milestones.]
Then came the System’s final explanation.
[The System encourages healthy Yandere wives.]
A long silence, then Luke face-palmed himself. "What the heck is a healthy Yandere?"
"Since when have Yanderes become healthy?"
At this the system showed an innocent smile.
Upon this, Luke’s mouth twitched violently.
Slowly, he raised a trembling finger toward the floating System screen.
"You seriously don’t want me to live anymore."
The System let out a dramatic sigh.
[Sigh, Luke, listen carefully.]

chapters.title: Chapter 223: A Legendary Mage Answered My Call!
paragraphs: Its tone suddenly changed. Instead of its usual teasing voice.
It sounded like an older brother patiently explaining something to a clueless younger sibling.
[Have you ever wondered why your very first Titan was Nyx?]
Luke blinked.
"Now, what does that have to do with this?" He couldn’t see the connection at all.
The System sighed again.
[Think about it.]
[Not only were you given Nyx.]
[You were also given Shadow of Nyx.]
[A clone that is, for all practical purposes, another you.]
Luke’s expression slowly changed.
As the System continued. He finally began understanding where this conversation was heading.
[Just sacrifice one or two clones here and there.]
[Just chill, buddy.]
Luke paused for a moment.
Then he slowly nodded. "That actually makes sense."
Even though.
The moment he imagined his other self tied to a chair—
"No."
Luke immediately shook his head.
This is a fantasy world.
Think bigger.
The next scene in his imagination changed instantly.
His clone was hanging above a sea of boiling lava, chained to a massive rock.
Meanwhile.
His dragon wife sat on a nearby cliff, gently swinging her legs while watching him with a sweet smile.
"Luke, If you can’t belong to me..."
"Then you can’t belong to anyone else."
She slowly licked one of her crimson claws.
Fresh blood still dripped from its tip.
Apparently.
It belonged to several unfortunate women who had dared to approach him.
The dragoness only smiled more brightly.
"They should’ve known better."
Luke shivered.
Enough.
He forcefully erased the horrifying image from his mind before it could become any more ridiculous.
Taking a deep breath.
He returned his attention to the System.
The System, however, seemed unusually excited.
[Exactly!]
[Now you’re getting it!]
Then the System shamelessly declared,
[So, Luke!]
[This System demands Yanderes!]
[Bring more and more Yanderes!]
A brief pause.
Then its laughter echoed through Luke’s mind.
[HAHAHAHAHAHA!!]
[LET THE WORLD BURN!!!]
"Was the last part really necessary?" Luke looked at the System with a thoroughly speechless expression.
The System didn’t even bother answering.
It simply continued laughing.
[Kekeke.]
Luke shook his head. "There really is something wrong with you."
Deciding not to waste any more energy arguing. He shifted his attention back to the milestone rewards.
As for the daily rewards from the previous seven days.
He didn’t even bother checking them.
They were nothing more than Mana Crystals, some gold coins, a few ores, and cultivation resources suitable only for Iron Knights.
There was no point spending precious 1,000× or 10,000× charges upgrading those.
It would be a complete waste.
Meanwhile.
The System was still immersed in its own fantasy.
[Kekekeke...]
It almost seemed to be imagining Luke’s future yandere wives setting the entire world ablaze.
After discovering his clone instead of the real him.
Luke decided it was healthier not to ask what was going on inside the System’s nonexistent head.
Instead.
He opened the newly unlocked feature.
Monthly Claim.
The System interface immediately changed.
There on the reward selection screen. Two different Monthly Claims appeared before him.
One looked completely ordinary.
The other had a distinct Special tag attached to it.
"Let’s see." Luke rubbed his hands together. "What exactly makes this one so special?"
Without hesitating he selected the Special Monthly Claim.
A new screen immediately appeared before him.
Luke quickly read through it. His eyes slowly widened.
"A B-Rank reward?"
The special claim allowed him to freely choose any B-Rank reward.
Sadly, it completely ignored the normal Return system.
No matter whether his current Return was 1×, 1,000×, or 10,000×. It wouldn’t affect this reward at all.
So with curiousity, he returned and opened the ordinary Monthly Claim.
A few seconds later.
"Wait!" His face froze. "Seriously?"
He couldn’t help cursing under his breath.
The description clearly stated—
Monthly Claims cannot be upgraded using the Return multiplier.
Instead.
The Return only increased the quantity of the selected reward.
Luke pinched the bridge of his nose.
"So that’s how it works."
In other words.
He could freely choose any reward between G-Rank and D-Rank, matching Aurielle’s current realm.
Then whatever Return he had accumulated would simply multiply the number of that reward.
For example. If he had accumulated 30,000× worth of daily charges.
Choosing a D-Rank reward would immediately grant him 30,000 copies of it.
Although it was a little disappointing. Luke couldn’t really complain.
Being able to choose the exact reward he wanted every month was already an unbelievable advantage.
[See?] The System’s proud voice echoed inside his mind.
[Didn’t I tell you?]
[System features are always the best.]
Luke smiled and nodded.
"Yeah."
"This time, I’ll admit it."
Even without the ability to upgrade the Monthly Claim itself. Its usefulness was unquestionable.
Being able to choose exactly what he needed every month was far more valuable than relying entirely on luck.
The ordinary claim had already been decided.
Bronze Knight Tempering Potions.
Those would greatly speed up his cultivation before his upcoming journey to the capital.
That decision required no further thought.
Now only one choice remained.
The Special Monthly Claim.
A reward that could directly grant him any B-Rank thing.
Luke folded his arms.
"Let’s see." He closed his eyes and began carefully considering every possibility.
Several ideas flashed through his mind before he rejected them one after another.
Minutes quietly passed.
Then Luke slowly opened his eyes.
A decisive smile appeared on his face. "I’ve decided."
Without the slightest hesitation. He selected his choice.
[Selected Reward: Summon One B-Rank Being.]
A confirmation window immediately appeared.
[Summon B-Rank Being?]
[Yes] [No]
Luke stared at the screen.
Then the corner of his mouth twitched.
"System."
"Why can’t I choose the type? Or at least the gender?"
His complaint was answered almost instantly.
A new notification appeared.
[Luke.]
[With this update, this far you can make choice.]
After that, the System paused. Then another line slowly appeared.
[As for choosing the gender. That is not possible.]
Luke sighed. "I figured."
Then the System revealed its reason.
[Just imagine this.]
[Suppose you summon an macho man.]
[He might end up stealing most of your charm.]
Luke stared blankly at the screen.
"That’s your reason?"
Luke didn’t even know how to respond.
Finally, he pinched the bridge of his nose.
"Whatever."
"I’m done arguing with you."
Without wasting another second. He reached out and pressed Yes.
The confirmation window disappeared.
In its place a new notification slowly materialized.
[Summoning B-Rank Being...]
"With this." Luke let out a relieved breath.
"The territory’s safety should reach an entirely different level."
Although he was confident that, after advancing to the Silver Knight Realm, he might be capable of escaping from a Platinum Knight.
That confidence applied only to himself.
Not to Blackstone, no to Aurielle. And definetly not to everyone else he wanted to protect.
Jasper had indeed promised to send a Platinum Knight.
But Luke had never truly relied on that promise.
If the worst possible situation occurred. That powerhouse would naturally prioritize protecting himself.
There was no guarantee he would risk his life for Aurielle, Aurora, or the rest of Blackstone.
Luke couldn’t blame him for that.
After all they weren’t family.
Which was precisely why Luke wanted his own Platinum-rank guardian.
Then—
The System’s notification appeared.
[Congratulations.]
[You have obtained a B-Rank Being.]
[Arcane Core Mage.]

chapters.title: Chapter 224: The Queen Who Dreamed Worlds!
paragraphs: "Huh?" Luke blinked in surprise.
An unexpected smile spread across his face.
"A mage?"
For a long time, almost every powerful summon he had received had been a knight.
To the point where Luke had started believing the System simply refused to give him any other class anymore, except earlier, bloodline warriors.
Yet now after so many summons. He had finally obtained one.
An Arcane Core Mage.
Which immediately rose his excitement to another level.
Because unlike knights. Mages specialized in overwhelming area destruction.
And an Arcane Core Mage. Stood at the very same realm as a Platinum Knight.
Just imagining that level of magical firepower made Luke’s heart race.
Without another moment of hesitation.
He raised his hand.
"Summon."
[Summoning... Theia Yvette: Arcane Core Mage...]
"Theia." Luke quietly repeated the name.
A smile appeared on his face. "That’s a beautiful name."
Unlike previous summons. This one wasn’t completed instantly.
One minute passed.
Then two.
Three. Four. Even after five minutes. The summoning process was still ongoing.
"Hm?" Upon this, Luke raised an eyebrow.
"So Platinum-rank summons really do take longer."
Just as he finished speaking—
WHOOOOOM!
A purple magic circle suddenly unfolded beneath his feet.
Intricate runes rotated one after another, while ancient arcane symbols lit up across its surface.
The surrounding Aether rapidly gathered toward its center.
A silhouette slowly emerged from the dazzling light.
WHOOSSH!
A violent burst of magical energy exploded outward.
Which results, the surrounding wind was swept away in every direction.
Luke’s clothes fluttered wildly.
Moments later. The magic circle gradually faded.
Standing where it had been.
Was a woman.
She wore an elegant robe of deep violet embroidered with intricate silver runes that shimmered faintly under the sun-light.
Her long, lustrous purple hair flowed gently behind her with the lingering wind.
Her dark emerald eyes calmly observed Luke.
They were neither cold nor warm.
Luke unconsciously held his breath.
’She’s beautiful.’
Beautiful wasn’t enough to describe her.
She possessed an elegant, almost ethereal charm that made her seem untouchable.
The kind of woman people would instinctively mistake for a goddess or an archmage.
Even Luke had to admit. Her appearance surpassed almost every woman he had met.
Including...
Aurielle.
That thought made him inwardly cough.
’I’m definitely not saying that out loud.’
If Aurielle ever learned he had compared another woman’s appearance to hers. Luke was fairly certain.
His clones would have a very difficult future.
[Kekeke.] The System sounded unusually pleased.
[Luke, once a being reaches C-Rank and above. B-Rank, A-Rank, S-Rank, and beyond.]
[Their bodies undergo a true metamorphosis with every major realm.]
[Imperfections are gradually removed.]
[By the higher realms. Their bodies naturally become flawless.]
"No wonder." Luke finally understood.
It wasn’t simply that Theia was beautiful.
Her very existence had been refined through transformations.
After calming his thoughts. Luke put on a welcoming smile.
And just as he was about to greet her—
She spoke first.
"Greetings, my liege." Her voice was composed and elegant.
Unlike every summon he had met before.
There was respect. But not overwhelming reverence.
She hadn’t called him Master.
Only...
Liege.
Luke’s smile paused for the briefest moment.
’System, what’s going on?’ A trace of caution appeared in his heart.
The System had always insisted that every summon would possess loyalty.
If that wasn’t true. A B-Rank summon becoming hostile would be catastrophic.
The System calmly replied.
[Luke, She is completely loyal.]
Luke quietly listened.
[However. She is a higher-ranked being.]
[Compared to your previous summons. She possesses far greater self-awareness from the moment she is summoned.]
[Loyalty and individuality are not mutually exclusive.]
Luke slowly relaxed.
"I see." That explanation made perfect sense.
If every high-ranking summon behaved like an emotionless puppet. That would have been stranger.
’As long as her loyalty remained unquestionable. Her personality didn’t matter.’
So Luke smiled warmly once more.
"Welcome to Blackstone."
"Theia."
At this Theia gave a graceful nod. "It is my honor to serve, my liege."
Without saying anything further. Luke shifted his attention toward the translucent screen that had already appeared before him.
It was time to see the status of his first B-Rank summon.
While Luke focused on the status panel before him. Theia remained completely silent.
She made no attempt to interrupt him. Nor did she ask where she was.
Her dark emerald eyes quietly wandered across the surroundings, calmly observing everything within sight.
The distant hills.
The rich flow of mana in the air.
The towering trees.
The Mana Well.
Even the damaged area left behind by the earlier explosion.
Nothing escaped her notice.
[Summon: Theia Yvette (B-rank)]
[Origin Skill - S-rank (Dream Well.)]
📜 THE LORE
The Dream Well is the mind of a sleeping queen.

In a forgotten age, there was a queen who could dream reality into existence. She created palaces, armies, and entire kingdoms from her dreams. Her imagination was boundless—she could conjure anything she envisioned with a single thought.

But she grew tired of her power. She had seen empires rise and fall at her whim. She had created worlds, only to watch them crumble. She had become bored with the world she had shaped. So she created the Dream Well and poured her mind into it.

Now she sleeps, her dreams drifting through the well, waiting for someone to draw from them. Some say she is not truly asleep—that she is waiting for the right moment to wake. Others say she is dreaming still, creating worlds within her own mind, worlds that no one will ever see.
Those who touch the Dream Well are touching the mind of a sleeping god-queen. They draw from her imagination, her power, her endless dreams. But they must be careful—she may wake.
Gulp.
Luke unconsciously swallowed.
His eyes slowly lifted from the status panel toward Theia.
She was still standing quietly in the distance.
Her gaze rested upon Blackstone City.
A trace of curiosity flickered across her emerald eyes, as though she had already become absorbed in her own thoughts.
She looked perfectly calm. Perfectly harmless.
Yet after reading her status. Luke couldn’t look at her the same way anymore.
’System! why the heck did you summon Pandora-type existences?’ He couldn’t help cursing inwardly.
The System answered as casually as ever.
[I already told you.]
[The rewards themselves aren’t decided by me.]
Its carefree tone made it sound as though Theia wasn’t terrifying in the slightest.
Luke’s eyelid twitched.
"Easy for you to say." He muttered under his breath.
After all, if something went wrong. The System certainly wasn’t the one who would have to deal with an Arcane Core Mage.
Deciding there was no point arguing anymore. Luke simply shook his head.
"Whatever." He lowered his gaze once again.
This time his attention shifted toward the section he was most interested in.
Origin Abilities.
[🧠 PASSIVE ABILITY]
Dream Sight: Sees the dreams of all beings within 100 kilometers. Knows their desires, fears, and secrets
Luke stared at the description for several long seconds.
Then he slowly narrowed his eyes.
"That’s completely broken." A passive ability like this was almost impossible to defend against.
As long as someone remained within a hundred kilometers. Theia could potentially uncover their true intentions.
Whether they wished to betray him, Assassinate him Or secretly support him.
